definition_zh: 前景；展望；观点；看法；景色；视野
definition_en: the way a situation is likely to develop, a person's settled attitude towards life or a subject, or the view seen from a particular place
core_image: 站在窗前向外望，远处的地平线和压低的云一起收进眼里
scene: 清晨的田埂上，老人蹲下去捏了一把土，又抬头看天边压着的云。The outlook for the harvest is poor this year.
sceneCN: 这里的 outlook 是「前景、展望」（第 1 个义项：事情可能的发展方向）；句意为今年收成的前景不佳。图中可辨识物件：田埂、捏碎的土块、天边的云。

derivatives.zh: 由 look 与 out 换序构成的复合词，义为「瞭望台；守望」
由 over（在上方）与 look 复合而成，义为「俯瞰；忽视」
由 on 与 look 加表示「做某事的人」的 -er 构成，义为「旁观者」

senses.title: The likely future of a situation
senses.definition: the way a situation is likely to develop, especially in business, farming or public affairs
senses.definitionCN: 事情可能的发展方向，尤用于商业、农业或公共事务
senses.example: The outlook for the harvest is poor this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年收成的前景不佳。
senses.why: Outlook is out plus look: the word first named a place to watch from, and what a watcher could see ahead turned into the future that is coming towards everyone.
senses.whyCN: outlook 是 out 加 look：这个词最初指一个可以向外张望的位置，而守望者能望见的前方，就变成了正在朝所有人走来的未来。

senses.title: A settled way of thinking about life
senses.definition: a person's general attitude to life, or to a particular subject such as work or money
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对生活或某个话题（如工作、金钱）的总体态度
senses.example: She has a cheerful outlook on life.
senses.exampleCN: 她对生活抱着乐观的态度。
senses.why: The direction in which someone looks decides what that person notices, so the same noun moves from the eye to the mind and names a habitual point of view.
senses.whyCN: 一个人朝哪个方向看，决定了他会注意到什么，于是这个名词从眼睛转到心里，用来指一种习惯性的看法。

senses.title: The view seen from a place
senses.definition: what can be seen from a particular place, especially open country, a bay or a hillside
senses.definitionCN: 从某处望出去所能看到的景物，尤指开阔的田野、海湾或山坡
senses.example: The room has a wide outlook over the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间能望见开阔的海湾景色。
senses.why: Long before the word had anything to do with the future, it named the act of looking out and the scene that rewarded it, and that concrete sense still survives in descriptions of rooms and hills.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词和未来扯上关系之前很久，它先指「向外张望」这个动作以及由此看到的景象，这一具体义项仍活在描写房间与山丘的说法里。

intro.en: Outlook is a compound of two Old English words, out and look, recorded as a noun in the seventeenth century; it moved from a watching place to a view, and then to the future and to a state of mind.
intro.cn: outlook 由 out 与 look 两个古英语词复合而成，十七世纪才有名词记录；它从「守望之处」转到「眼前之景」，再转到「未来的走向」与「心里的态度」。

items.en: Lōcian meant to look or to see, and it is the direct ancestor of the modern verb look.
items.cn: lōcian 意为看、望，是现代动词 look 的直接祖先。

items.en: Ūt meant out or outward, and it joined verbs and nouns to show movement away from the inside.
items.cn: ūt 意为向外、朝外，常与动词和名词结合，表示由内向外。

items.en: The earliest noun outlook named a place or a post from which someone kept watch, and the act of watching from it.
items.cn: 最早的名词 outlook 指供人守望的位置或岗位，也指在那里张望这件事。

items.en: From what one sees at a watching place, the word widened to a view of land or sea, and then to the prospects that lie ahead.
items.cn: 从在守望处所见之物出发，词义先扩展到眼前的陆地或海面之景，再扩展到前方等待的种种可能。

items.en: Modern English keeps the landscape sense and adds the future sense, the likely course of events, and the mental sense, a settled way of looking at life.
items.cn: 现代英语保留风景义，又加上未来义（事情可能的走向）与精神义（看待生活的固定态度）。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on look or spelled close to it; the near-meaning group collects words for prospects, angles of thought and visible views.
note.cn: 形近组收由 look 构成或拼写相近的词；近义组收表示前景、思考角度与眼前景色的词。

entries.definition: To direct the eyes towards something.
entries.definitionCN: 把目光投向某物；看。

entries.definition: A place or a person that keeps watch.
entries.definitionCN: 守望的地方或守望的人。

entries.definition: To look down on something from above, or to fail to notice it.
entries.definitionCN: 从上方俯视，或未注意到。

entries.definition: A shop or an opening through which goods or water leave.
entries.definitionCN: 让货物或水流出的店铺或出口；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The possibility that something, good or bad, will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 某事（无论好坏）将要发生的可能性；前景。

entries.definition: A particular way of thinking about something.
entries.definitionCN: 思考某事的特定角度。

entries.definition: What can be seen from a place, or an opinion held about something.
entries.definitionCN: 从某处看到的景物，或对某事的看法。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking or feeling about something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物的固定想法或感受；态度。

normalIntro.en: Outlook is two Old English words joined, so the hooks keep the picture of eyes turned outward and what they meet at the far end.
normalIntro.cn: outlook 是两个古英语词的结合，所以记忆钩子始终保留「目光朝外转、在远处遇到什么」的画面。

normal.en: Outlook is simply out plus look, so the spelling itself shows the direction the eyes are turned.
normal.cn: outlook 就是 out 加 look，拼写本身已经标出目光朝向哪边。

normal.en: The watching-place sense came first, which is why a hilltop hotel can still advertise its outlook over the bay.
normal.cn: 守望之处的意思最先出现，所以山顶旅馆至今仍用这个词来宣传它望向海湾的景致。

normal.en: The weather outlook on the evening news borrows the same word for what the sky is likely to do next.
normal.cn: 晚间新闻里的天气展望也借用这个词，指天色接下来可能的走向。

normal.en: An outlook on life is not scenery but the direction a mind keeps looking in, which is why the phrase sounds slightly more settled than opinion.
normal.cn: an outlook on life 说的不是风景，而是一个头脑长期望去的方向，所以这个说法比 opinion 更显得稳固。

normal.en: Lookout reverses the two parts and keeps the same watching, so the pair is easy to confuse in reading.
normal.cn: lookout 把两部分调了个个儿，守望的意思没变，所以阅读时这一对很容易看混。

abstract.en: A word for the direction of a gaze suggests that a person's future is partly a matter of where that person chooses to look.
abstract.cn: 一个表示目光方向的词说明：一个人的未来，有一部分取决于他选择往哪里看。

abstract.en: Prospects are shared and measurable, while an outlook belongs to one mind and can be changed without anything outside changing.
abstract.cn: 前景是共享的、可以衡量的，而心态属于某一个头脑，外部什么都没变，它也可能已经变了。

abstract.en: Every window frames a view, and every view quietly tells the viewer what to expect next.
abstract.cn: 每一扇窗都框住一片景，而每一片景都在悄悄告诉看的人接下来会怎样。

examples.en: The outlook for the harvest is poor this year.
examples.cn: 今年收成的前景不佳。

examples.en: She has a cheerful outlook on life.
examples.cn: 她对生活抱着乐观的态度。

examples.en: The room has a wide outlook over the bay.
examples.cn: 这个房间能望见开阔的海湾景色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特路克」——奥特站在路口向外望，望见的是往后的事；记住 outlook 是前景、观点。

root: 由古英语 ūt（向外）与 lōcian（看）复合而成，十七世纪出现，最初指「向外张望的守望之处」，后指所见之景、事情的前景以及看待事物的态度；look 属日耳曼语词，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a looking outward; the senses divide into what lies ahead, the attitude that decides what one notices, and the view actually in front of the eyes.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是向外张望；义项按「前方将发生的事」「决定你注意到什么的态度」「眼前真实的景物」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing at a window looking out, the far horizon and the low cloud gathered into one view.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在窗前向外望，远处的地平线与压低的云一起收进眼里。

branches.en: a field whose harvest may fail
branches.cn: 可能歉收的一片田

branches.en: a person who expects good things
branches.cn: 总期待好事的一个人

branches.en: a window filled with water and sky
branches.cn: 装满水光与天色的窗子

branches.en: one noun for a view and for what is coming
branches.cn: 同一个名词，既指眼前之景，也指将来之事

branches.en: the eye turned outward and the mind turned with it
branches.cn: 眼睛朝外，心也跟着朝外

intro.en: The word is two Old English pieces, an adverb of direction and a verb of seeing, fused into a single noun that has kept both the eye and the future in view.
intro.cn: 这个词由两块古英语成分构成，一个表方向，一个表看，合成一个名词，同时把眼睛与未来都留在视野里。

latinIntro.en: Outlook is built entirely from Old English words, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound.
latinIntro.cn: outlook 完全由古英语词构成，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a person who watches without taking part

definition_zh: 产量；产出；输出；输出数据；生产
definition_en: the amount produced by a person, machine, or system; data or energy sent out; to produce or send out
core_image: 工厂传送带末端，成品一件件被放到外面
scene: 工厂升级设备后，工程师站在传送带旁盯着成品箱。Hourly output rose from 120 units to 180 units in the first week.
sceneCN: 这里 output 是“单位时间内的产量”（第 1 个义项：生产出来的数量）；句意：每小时的产量在第一周就从 120 件提高到 180 件。图中可辨识物件：传送带、成品箱、白板、秒表；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 放；置；表达
输入；投入（in + put）
吞吐量；处理能力
输出设备；输出者（技术语境）
外港；输出港

senses.title: The quantity produced
senses.definition: the amount of goods or work produced in a given time
senses.definitionCN: 在给定时间内生产出的货物或工作量
senses.example: The factory doubled its output in three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂在三年内把产量翻了一倍。
senses.why: Output began in 1839 as a technical term of the iron and coal trades: the material put out of the works. The word does not name the goods themselves but the quantity that comes out of the process.
senses.whyCN: output 在 1839 年作为钢铁与煤炭行业的技术词出现：被“放到外面”的材料。它命名的不是货物本身，而是从过程中出来的数量。

senses.title: Energy delivered by a device
senses.definition: the power, energy, or signal that a machine or system delivers
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统输送出的功率、能量或信号
senses.example: The solar array has an output of five kilowatts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个太阳能阵列的输出功率为五千瓦。
senses.why: By 1884 output named 'energy produced by a device or system'. The industrial image is kept, but what comes out is now electricity or a signal rather than coal.
senses.whyCN: 到 1884 年，output 指“设备或系统产生的能量”。工业画面保留下来，只是出来的东西变成了电或信号，而不是煤。

senses.title: Data produced by a computer
senses.definition: the data, results, or display that a computer sends to a user or another device
senses.definitionCN: 计算机发送给用户或其他设备的数据、结果或显示内容
senses.example: Check the output for error messages.
senses.exampleCN: 检查输出里有没有错误信息。
senses.why: Computing adopts the same schema: a program takes input in and puts output out. The metaphor of a factory becomes a flow of characters on a terminal.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用同一图式：程序把输入拿进来，把输出放出去。工厂的比喻变成了终端上流动的字符。

senses.title: Work produced by a researcher or artist
senses.titleCN: 研究者或创作者的产出
senses.definition: the amount or quality of work that a person, team, or field produces
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团队或领域所生产工作的数量或质量
senses.example: Her research output rose after she left teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 离开教学岗位后，她的研究产出增加了。
senses.why: The word extends from things to work: papers, books, and paintings are also what comes out of a process. Output measures volume, while quality is a separate question.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从实物延伸到作品：论文、书、画也是过程里出来的东西。output 衡量的是数量，质量则是另一个问题。

senses.title: To produce or emit something
senses.definition: to produce, generate, or send out goods, data, energy, or sound
senses.definitionCN: 生产、产生或发出货物、数据、能量或声音
senses.example: The speakers output a low hum.
senses.exampleCN: 扬声器发出低低的嗡鸣。
senses.why: The verb 'to produce' appears in 1858, long after the noun. What was a thing at the end of a process becomes an action: the system outputs whatever it sends forth.
senses.whyCN: 动词“生产”义出现于 1858 年，比名词晚得多。原本位于过程末端的“东西”变成了动作：系统输出它所送出的任何内容。

senses.title: Obsolete: to expel or exclude
senses.definition: in older use, to expel or shut something out
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，表示逐出或排除某物
senses.example: The older verb meant to put a person out of a place.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的动词义是“把人赶出一个地方”。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from the mid-14c. in the sense 'expel, exclude', which is now obsolete. The literal 'put out' is the seed from which both 'produce' and 'exclude' grew in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 该动词在 14 世纪中期记录的义项是“逐出、排除”，现已废弃。字面的“放到外面”是一颗种子，向两个方向长出了“生产”和“排除”。

senses.title: Creative or athletic yield
senses.definition: the total amount of creative work or performance produced over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内产生的创作或表演总量
senses.example: The band's output slowed during the tour.
senses.exampleCN: 巡演期间乐队的产出放缓了。
senses.why: Output treats creative work as measurable production. The image is quantitative: a career can be counted like a factory shift, even if the value of each piece cannot.
senses.whyCN: output 把创作当成可测量的生产。这个画面是数量化的：一段职业生涯可以像工厂班次一样被计数，尽管每件作品的价值无法这样计算。

senses.title: A signal or terminal that sends data
senses.titleCN: 发送数据的信号或端口
senses.definition: an output terminal, port, or channel through which a device sends signals
senses.definitionCN: 设备借以发送信号的输出端、端口或通道
senses.example: Connect the monitor to the video output.
senses.exampleCN: 把显示器接到视频输出端口。
senses.why: Here output names not the data but the doorway it leaves through. The noun shifts from what comes out to the place of exit, a common pattern in technical vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 这里 output 指的不是数据，而是数据离开的那扇门。名词从“出来的东西”转到“出口的位置”，这是技术词汇里常见的转义方式。

intro.en: Output is a native English compound, first a technical trade term and then a general word for production. No Latin root is involved.
intro.cn: output 是英语本族复合词，先是行业技术词，后成为一般的“产出”词。不涉及拉丁词根。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the mid-14c. meaning 'to expel, exclude', a literal 'put out'. This sense is now obsolete.
items.cn: 动词记录于 14 世纪中期，义为“逐出、排除”，即字面的“放到外面”。这一义项现已废弃。

items.en: The noun appears meaning 'quantity of material put out or produced in a given time'. Until about 1880 it was a technical term in the iron and coal trade.
items.cn: 名词出现，义为“在给定时间内产出或生产的材料数量”。直到约 1880 年，它都是钢铁与煤炭行业的技术词。

items.en: The verb gains the modern sense 'to produce', while the 1884 noun sense 'energy produced by a device or system' follows.
items.cn: 动词获得现代义“生产”；随后 1884 年名词出现“设备或系统产生的能量”这一义项。

items.en: Computing makes output half of the input/output pair. Research and economics extend it to papers, data, and national production.
items.cn: 计算机领域让 output 成为 input/output 这对概念的一半。科研与经济学把它扩展到论文、数据与国家生产。

items.en: The compound stays transparent: out (forth) + put (place, thrust). Something is placed outward, and that outward placement is the output.
items.cn: 这个复合词始终透明：out（向外）+ put（放置、推）。某物被放到外面，而这次“向外放置”就是 output。

note.en: The look-alike group separates out- compounds; the near-meaning group separates quantity from result and from input.
note.cn: 形近组区分其他 out- 复合词；近义组区分“数量”“结果”与“投入”。

entries.definition: the result that comes out of a process. It is the end state, not the quantity produced.
entries.definitionCN: 过程产生的结果。它是终态，不是生产数量。

entries.definition: what is put into a system: materials, data, or effort. It is the mirror image of output.
entries.definitionCN: 投入系统的材料、数据或人力。它是 output 的镜像。

entries.definition: a small military or trading settlement far from the main base. It is a place put out, not a quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 远离主基地的军事或贸易据点。它是被放到外面的地点，不是数量。

entries.definition: the beginning of something. It marks the start, the opposite end from output's product.
entries.definitionCN: 某事的开端。它标记起点，与 output 的产物处在相反的一端。

entries.definition: the act or process of making goods. It names the activity; output names the amount that results.
entries.definitionCN: 制造商品的行为或过程。它命名活动；output 命名由此产生的数量。

entries.definition: the amount produced, especially by land or an investment. It often implies a return on effort or capital.
entries.definitionCN: 产量，尤指土地或投资带来的收益。它常含“投入的回报”之意。

entries.definition: output measured per unit of input, such as per hour or per worker. It is a ratio, not a total.
entries.definitionCN: 每单位投入（如每小时或每人）所对应的产出。它是比率，不是总量。

entries.definition: what follows from an action or process. It can be abstract; output is usually measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 由行动或过程产生的东西。它可以是抽象的；output 通常可测量。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on 'put out', then three abstract images.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个围绕“放到外面”的钩子，再用三个抽象画面。

normal.en: output = put out: whatever the system places outside itself.
normal.cn: output＝put out：系统放到自己外面的东西。

normal.en: input goes in, output comes out: the same put, opposite doors.
normal.cn: input 进，output 出：同一个 put，方向相反的两扇门。

normal.en: A factory's output is counted in units per hour, like a heartbeat monitor.
normal.cn: 工厂的 output 按每小时多少件来计数，像心跳监护仪上的数字。

normal.en: Computer output is what appears on the screen after the program has put it out.
normal.cn: 计算机的 output 就是程序“放到外面”后出现在屏幕上的内容。

normal.en: Audio output is the sound that leaves the speaker.
normal.cn: audio output 是离开扬声器的声音。

abstract.en: Output measures how much a system gives to the world, not how much it is worth.
abstract.cn: output 衡量一个系统给了世界多少，而不是它值多少。

abstract.en: Every system has a door: what goes in is input, what leaves is output.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都有一扇门：进去的是 input，离开的是 output。

abstract.en: A person can be counted like a factory and still be unmeasurable as a mind.
abstract.cn: 一个人可以像工厂一样被计数，却仍然无法作为一个心灵被测量。

examples.en: The mine's output fell after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，这座矿的产量下降了。

examples.en: Please save the program's output to a text file.
examples.cn: 请把程序的输出保存到一个文本文件。

examples.en: The new turbine outputs twice as much power as the old one.
examples.cn: 新涡轮机的输出功率是旧机的两倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: out（向外）+ put（放）→ 放到外面的东西 → 产出、输出

root: 英语本族复合词：out（向外）+ put（放置）；1839 年见于钢铁与煤炭行业，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from industrial quantity, to energy, computer data, creative work, and finally the act of emitting or the port that emits.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从工业产量，走到能量、计算机数据、创作成果，最后落到“发出”的动作或发出数据的端口。

core.en: Finished goods placed outside the factory gate
core.cn: 成品被放到工厂大门之外

branches.en: Measured production: goods per hour, or power delivered by a device.
branches.cn: 可测量的生产：每小时多少件，或设备输送的功率。

branches.en: Computer output and the port it leaves through.

senses.title: The act of setting out on a journey
senses.definition: the act of starting a journey or setting off, the oldest sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 动身开始一段行程的行为，是这个词最老的义项
senses.example: The travellers made an early outset before the roads grew busy.
senses.exampleCN: 旅人们在道路变拥挤之前早早启程。
senses.why: Outset began as the noun of the phrase set out, which meant to leave on a journey, so the oldest sense still carries the picture of feet crossing a doorway.
senses.whyCN: outset 起初是短语 set out（出发、启程）的名词形式，所以最老的义项仍带着「双脚跨出门槛」的画面。

senses.title: The beginning of an event or period
senses.definition: the point in time at which an event, a meeting or a period begins
senses.definitionCN: 一件事、一场会议或一段时期开始的那一刻
senses.example: At the outset of the meeting, nobody wanted to speak first.
senses.exampleCN: 会议刚开始时，没人愿意先开口。
senses.why: Once the noun named the moment of leaving, it could name the opening moment of anything at all, and that is how a word about journeys became a word about meetings and wars.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词本指「离开」的那一刻，它就能指任何事情的开头一刻，于是关于行程的词变成了关于会议与战争的词。

senses.title: The starting point a process grows from
senses.definition: the first stage of a process, plan or career, seen as what everything later grows out of
senses.definitionCN: 过程、计划或事业的第一个阶段，后来的东西都由它长出来
senses.example: The design was too costly from the outset.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计从一开始就太昂贵。
senses.why: If the word marks the first moment of an event, it can also mark the point a process starts from, which is why from the outset means from the very first stage and not merely at some early time.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出一件事的最初一瞬，它也能标出一个过程起步的那一点，所以 from the outset 指从最初阶段起，而不只是某个较早的时候。

intro.en: Outset is a noun made from the phrasal verb set out, to start a journey; it appeared in English in the sixteenth century and now lives almost only inside the fixed phrases at the outset and from the outset.
intro.cn: outset 是由短语动词 set out（出发）转成的名词，十六世纪出现在英语中，如今几乎只活在 at the outset 与 from the outset 这两个固定说法里。

items.en: Settan meant to set, to place or to cause to sit, and it is the source of the modern verb set.
items.cn: settan 意为放置、使坐下，是现代动词 set 的来源。

items.en: Ūt meant out, and with a verb of movement it marked the point of leaving a place.
items.cn: ūt 意为向外，与表示移动的动词连用时标出离开某处的那一点。

items.en: The phrase set out meant to begin a journey or an undertaking, and it was common in travel and in accounts of work.
items.cn: 短语 set out 意为启程或着手一项事务，在旅行记述与工作记录中很常见。

items.en: The noun outset was formed from that phrase and first meant a setting out, a departure.
items.cn: 名词 outset 由这个短语转成，最初指「出发、启程」。

items.en: The sense widened from a departure to the beginning of anything, and the word is now rare outside a few fixed phrases.
items.cn: 词义从「启程」扩展到任何事情的开头，如今除了少数固定说法以外已很少单独使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built on set; the near-meaning group collects nouns for a first point in time.
note.cn: 形近组收由 set 构成的复合词；近义组收表示时间上「最初一点」的名词。

normalIntro.en: Outset is a phrase turned into a noun, so its hooks keep the motion of stepping out of a door rather than any abstract idea of time.
normalIntro.cn: outset 是一句短语变成的名词，所以记忆钩子保留的是迈出门的那一步，而不是抽象的时间概念。

normal.en: The word is out plus set, and the pair simply reverses the phrase set out, to start a journey.
normal.cn: 这个词是 out 加 set，只是把短语 set out（出发）的次序调了过来。

normal.en: Nearly every modern use sits inside a fixed phrase, at the outset or from the outset, and the word rarely stands alone.
normal.cn: 现代用法几乎都嵌在 at the outset 或 from the outset 这样的固定说法里，这个词很少单独出现。

normal.en: Onset is the darker twin: an onset is usually something you dread, while an outset is simply a start.
normal.cn: onset 是它偏暗的孪生词：onset 通常是令人惧怕之事的发作，而 outset 只是平白的开头。

normal.en: Offset keeps set but turns the start into a counterweight, so the two compounds pull in opposite directions.
normal.cn: offset 也留着 set，却把「开始」变成了砝码，于是这两个复合词方向相反。

normal.en: Outset is formal and a little literary; a spoken sentence usually prefers start or beginning.
normal.cn: outset 偏正式、略带孩子气的文气；口语里通常更愿意用 start 或 beginning。

abstract.en: A word that began with stepping out of a door still reminds us that every beginning is also a move away from somewhere.
abstract.cn: 一个从迈出门槛起步的词提醒人：每一个开始同时也是离开某处的动作。

abstract.en: To say a plan was wrong from the outset is to claim the error was already there before the first step was taken.
abstract.cn: 说一个方案从一开始就错了，就是主张错误在迈出第一步之前已经存在。

abstract.en: Naming a start fixes a point in time, and after that point every account of events has somewhere to stand.
abstract.cn: 给开始命名，就是在时间里钉下一个点，此后每一种叙述都有了立足之处。

examples.cn: 会议刚开始时，没人愿意先开口。

examples.cn: 这个设计从一开始就太昂贵。

examples.en: The travellers made an early outset before the roads grew busy.
examples.cn: 旅人们在道路变拥挤之前早早启程。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是迈出门槛的那一步；义项按「启程本身」「一件事的开头一刻」「过程由之起步的最初阶段」分出。

core_image: 一排人站在同一条白线后面，只有一个人往前多迈了半步，肩膀露在外面
scene: 答辩结束后的教室里，评审把一份厚厚的报告翻到最后一页，抬头看了看站在讲台边的年轻人。The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
sceneCN: 这里的 outstanding 是「杰出的、出色的」（第 1 个义项：远高于一般水平）；句意为委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。图中可辨识物件：厚报告、讲台、评审的笔。

pos.zh: 杰出的；未付的；未完成的；显著的

senses.title: Much better than others
senses.definition: extremely good and clearly above the usual standard, so that people notice and praise it
senses.definitionCN: 极好而明显高于一般水平，因而被人注意并称赞
senses.example: The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。
senses.why: Outstanding is out plus standing: something that stands out from a row of others is seen first, and being seen first slowly turns into being admired.
senses.whyCN: outstanding 是 out 加 standing：在一排事物中「立在外面」的那一个最先被看见，而最先被看见就慢慢变成了被称赞。

senses.title: Still owed and not yet paid
senses.definition: of money or a bill, still owed to someone and not yet paid
senses.definitionCN: 指钱款或账单仍欠着别人、尚未付清
senses.example: The company has several outstanding debts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有几笔未偿债务。
senses.why: An unpaid debt is one that keeps standing there, unsettled, long after it should have been cleared, so the picture of standing out turns into standing open.
senses.whyCN: 一笔未付的债就是一直「立在那里」没有结清的账，本该了结却仍留在原处，于是「突出」的画面变成了「悬着未结」。

senses.title: Not yet done or settled
senses.definition: of work, problems or questions, not yet finished, answered or decided
senses.definitionCN: 指工作、问题或疑问尚未完成、回答或决定
senses.example: Two outstanding issues remain before the contract can be signed.
senses.exampleCN: 合同签署之前还有两个待解决的问题。
senses.why: Work that is finished leaves the desk; work still standing on it is the work not yet done, which is why the word covers pending tasks as well as unpaid money.
senses.whyCN: 做完的活会离开桌面，仍立在桌上的就是还没做完的活，所以这个词既能指待办的活儿，也能指没付的钱。

senses.title: Easily noticed, standing out clearly
senses.definition: clearly noticeable, especially as a feature of a thing, without any judgement of quality
senses.definitionCN: 明显引人注意，尤指某一事物的特征，并不含好坏评价
senses.example: The most outstanding feature of the design is its low roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计最突出的特点是它低矮的屋顶。
senses.why: Here the word keeps its literal picture: the part that stands out from the rest is the part the eye catches first, whether it is good, bad or merely different.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留的是字面画面：从其余部分里凸出来的那块，就是眼睛最先抓住的那块，不管它好、坏还是仅仅不同。

intro.en: Outstanding is out plus standing, first recorded in the sixteenth century for something that projects or stands clear; the senses of unpaid money and of excellence grew out of that physical picture.
intro.cn: outstanding 是 out 加 standing，十六世纪最早记录时指「凸出、立在外面」的东西；未付的款项与卓越这两个义项都从这个身体可感的画面长出来。

items.en: Standan meant to stand or to take up a position, and it is the source of the modern verb stand.
items.cn: standan 意为站立、占据一个位置，是现代动词 stand 的来源。

items.en: Standing named the act of standing and also a person's position or rank.
items.cn: standing 既指站立这个动作，也指一个人的位置或名次。

items.en: The compound outstanding was used for something that projects beyond a surface or stands clear of others.
items.cn: 复合词 outstanding 用来指超出某个表面、或在其他东西之外立着的事物。

items.en: The word widened in two directions: a debt still standing unpaid, and a person or work that stands above the rest.
items.cn: 这个词向两个方向扩展：一是仍「立着」未付的账，二是高出其余的人或作品。

items.en: Modern English uses it for excellence, for money not yet paid, for matters not yet settled, and for any feature that stands out.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示卓越、尚未支付的钱、尚未了结的事，以及任何突出的特征。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on stand and out; the near-meaning group collects words for excellence and for matters not yet closed.
note.cn: 形近组收由 stand 与 out 构成的词；近义组收表示卓越、以及表示「尚未了结」的词。

entries.definition: In a way that is far better than usual.
entries.definitionCN: 以远胜平常的方式；杰出地。

entries.definition: A person or thing that is clearly the best of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群中明显最好的那个人或那件东西。

entries.definition: A person's rank or reputation, or permanent rather than temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的地位或声望，或指常设而非临时的。

entries.definition: To grasp the meaning of something.
entries.definitionCN: 领会某事物的意思。

entries.definition: Extremely good of its kind.
entries.definitionCN: 同类中极好的。

entries.definition: Far better than usual, so that it forms an exception.
entries.definitionCN: 远胜平常，因而成为例外。

entries.definition: Of money or work, not yet paid for.
entries.definitionCN: 指钱款或劳动尚未得到支付。

entries.definition: Waiting to be decided or finished.
entries.definitionCN: 等待决定或完成的。

normalIntro.en: Outstanding rests on the plain physical fact of standing clear of a row, so its hooks keep that picture while the meanings travel towards money and praise.
normalIntro.cn: outstanding 建立在「从一排中站出来」这个朴素的实体画面之上，记忆钩子保留这个画面，让词义向金钱与赞美两头走。

normal.en: Outstanding is out plus standing, so the spelling already carries the picture of one thing standing clear of the rest.
normal.cn: outstanding 是 out 加 standing，拼写本身已经带着「某物立在其余之外」的画面。

normal.en: The money sense keeps the same picture: a debt stands there until it is settled, so it stays outstanding.
normal.cn: 金钱义保留同一画面：一笔债在结清之前一直立在原处，所以它是未付的。

normal.en: Outstandingly adds -ly and describes how well something was done, never how much money is owed.
normal.cn: outstandingly 加了 -ly，形容一件事做得多好，从不指欠了多少钱。

normal.en: Standout turns the two parts round for a person or thing that is obviously the best in a group.
normal.cn: standout 把两部分调过来，指一群中明显最好的那个人或那件东西。

normal.en: The old verb outstand is no longer used in ordinary English, so the adjective does the work alone.
normal.cn: 古动词 outstand 在现代英语里已不再使用，这项工作只由形容词独自承担。

abstract.en: A word built from standing suggests that excellence is often a matter of visibility: whatever stands out is noticed first.
abstract.cn: 一个从「站立」造出的词说明：卓越常常是可见度的问题，凡是站出来的，总被最先看到。

abstract.en: The same adjective covers praise and debt, which reminds us that what stands out can be either an honour or an obligation.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词兼指赞美与欠款，这提醒人：站出来的东西，既可能是荣誉，也可能是义务。

abstract.en: One word holds both the best work and the unpaid bill, because both are things that refuse to leave the desk.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装下最好的成果与未付的账单，因为这两样都不肯离开桌面。

examples.en: The committee gave her an award for outstanding research.
examples.cn: 委员会因她出色的研究而给她颁奖。

examples.en: The company has several outstanding debts.
examples.cn: 这家公司有几笔未偿债务。

examples.en: The most outstanding feature of the design is its low roof.
examples.cn: 这个设计最突出的特点是它低矮的屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特斯坦丁」——奥特站在队伍外面，站得最显眼；记住 outstanding 是杰出的、未付的。

root: 由 out（向外）与 standing（站立）复合，一般认为十六世纪出现，字面为「立在外面、凸出来」，由此分指显眼与卓越，以及仍「立着」未结清的账与未办完的事；stand 属日耳曼语词，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one thing standing clear of a row; the senses divide into being admired for it, money still standing unpaid, work still standing unfinished, and a feature that simply stands out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一样东西从一排之中站出来；义项按「因此被称赞」「钱仍立着未付」「活儿仍立着没完」「特征本身突出」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of people behind one white line, one of them half a step forward, a shoulder clear of the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排人站在同一条白线后面，只有一个人往前多迈了半步，肩膀露在外面。

branches.en: one report that the panel reads twice
branches.cn: 被评审读了两遍的那份报告

branches.en: a bill that stays on the desk for months
branches.cn: 在桌上压了几个月的账单

branches.en: two questions still waiting before a signature
branches.cn: 签字前仍悬着的两个问题

branches.en: a low roof that catches the eye at once
branches.cn: 一眼就抓住视线的低矮屋顶

branches.en: the same word for merit and for mere visibility
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指功绩，也指单纯的显眼

intro.en: The word joins a direction word to the old verb for standing, so its parts still say plainly: standing out of the line.
intro.cn: 这个词把方向词与表示站立的古老动词结合，各部分至今仍明白地说：站到队伍之外。

latinIntro.en: Outstanding is built from Old English standan and ūt, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound.
latinIntro.cn: outstanding 由古英语 standan 与 ūt 构成，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to be upright on the feet
forming a participle or a noun
a clearly superior person or thing

definition_zh: 向外的；朝外的；外表的；外部的；向外
definition_en: directed or moving away from the centre, concerning the outside rather than the inner nature, or in a direction away from something
core_image: 一件外套被翻过来，里子朝内，布面朝外，风从那一面吹过去
scene: 码头上的人把行李一件件搬上船，风从海面吹来，旗子朝同一个方向抖开。The ship's outward journey took three days.
sceneCN: 这里的 outward 是「向外的、出程的」（第 1 个义项：朝远离中心的方向）；句意为这艘船出航用了三天。图中可辨识物件：行李、船、抖开的旗。

derivatives.zh: 由 outward 加副词性 -s 构成，为英式英语常用的「向外」
由 outward 加 -ly 构成，义为「表面上；向外」

senses.title: Directed away from the centre
senses.definition: pointing or moving away from the inside or the centre of something
senses.definitionCN: 指向或移向某物的外部或远离中心的方向
senses.example: The ship's outward journey took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船出航用了三天。
senses.why: Outward is out plus the old suffix -weard, which means turned towards, so the word describes a thing turned to face away from where it started.
senses.whyCN: outward 是 out 加上古后缀 -weard（朝向），所以这个词描述的是「转过身去、背离起点」的方向。

senses.title: On the surface, not inside
senses.definition: relating to how something looks or appears rather than to what it is really like inside
senses.definitionCN: 指某物看起来的样子，而不是它内里真正的样子
senses.example: Outward calm hid a great deal of worry.
senses.exampleCN: 表面的平静掩藏了大量忧虑。
senses.why: If outward points to the outer side, it can also point to the outer layer of a person, and what lies on that layer is what others see rather than what is felt.
senses.whyCN: 既然 outward 指向外面那一侧，它也能指一个人的外层，而外层上的东西是别人看见的，不是他自己感到的。

senses.title: Belonging to the outside world
senses.definition: concerned with things outside a place, group or country, such as trade with other countries
senses.definitionCN: 指涉及某地、某群体或某国之外的事情，如与他国的贸易
senses.example: The country's outward trade grew faster than its home market.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的对外贸易增长快于国内市场。
senses.why: The same word of direction is used for whatever crosses a boundary towards others, so a country's dealings with the world outside become outward trade.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表方向的词也用来指越过边界、朝向他人的活动，于是一个国家与外部世界的往来就成了「对外贸易」。

senses.title: Away from the inside, used as an adverb
senses.definition: used as an adverb to describe movement away from a centre or away from oneself
senses.definitionCN: 作副词用，描述远离中心或远离自身的移动
senses.example: The doors open outward onto the courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 这些门向外开，通向院子。
senses.why: The adjective and the adverb share one form because the old suffix could end either kind of word, and English has kept both uses without adding anything.
senses.whyCN: 形容词与副词共用同一个形式，因为那个古老后缀既能构成形容词也能构成副词，英语把两种用法都留下来，没有再添加成分。

intro.en: Outward goes back to an Old English compound of ūt, out, and the suffix -weard, turned towards; English has kept it as both adjective and adverb, with the British adverb often written outwards.
intro.cn: outward 上溯古英语中由 ūt（向外）与后缀 -weard（朝向）构成的复合词；英语让它兼作形容词与副词，英式英语的副词常写作 outwards。

items.en: Ūt meant out, and it marked position or movement away from the inside of something.
items.cn: ūt 意为向外，标出远离某物内部的位置或移动。

items.en: The suffix -weard meant turned towards, and it also built words such as hāmweard, homeward.
items.cn: 后缀 -weard 意为「朝向」，也构成 hāmweard（向家）这类词。

items.en: Ūtweard described something turned or directed outward, and it worked as both adjective and adverb.
items.cn: ūtweard 形容朝外转或朝外指的东西，兼作形容词与副词。

items.en: Middle English kept the word for direction and extended it to the visible surface of a person or thing.
items.cn: 中古英语保留它的方向义，并扩展到一个人或一件东西可见的表面。

items.en: Modern English adds the social sense of outward-looking, and British usage often writes the adverb as outwards.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上 outward-looking 这种对外关注的社会义，英式用法常把副词写作 outwards。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words formed on the same -ward pattern; the near-meaning group collects words for what belongs to the outside or to appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收按 -ward 这一模式构成的词；近义组收表示「属于外部」或「属于表面」的词。

entries.definition: The British adverb form, meaning away from the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 英式副词形式，意为向外。

entries.definition: As it appears on the surface, whatever the truth inside.
entries.definitionCN: 就表面看来，不论内里如何。

entries.definition: Directed towards the inside, or felt privately inside.
entries.definitionCN: 朝向内部的，或内心感受到的。

entries.definition: On the way back towards home.
entries.definitionCN: 在回家的路上。

entries.definition: Belonging to or coming from the outside.
entries.definitionCN: 属于或来自外部的。

entries.definition: The outer surface of something, or outer.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外表面，或指外部的。

entries.definition: Further from the centre than something else.
entries.definitionCN: 比另一物离中心更远的。

entries.definition: Seeming true from what can be seen, though possibly not so.
entries.definitionCN: 从可见之处看似为真，但未必如此。

normalIntro.en: Outward is a direction word with an old suffix welded to it, so its hooks follow the line from an inside towards an outside.
normalIntro.cn: outward 是一个焊着古老后缀的方向词，记忆钩子顺着「从里面指向外面」的那条线走。

normal.en: Outward is out plus the old suffix -weard, turned towards, the same suffix that gives toward and homeward.
normal.cn: outward 是 out 加古后缀 -weard（朝向），toward 与 homeward 也出自同一个后缀。

normal.en: Because that suffix could mark either an adjective or an adverb, outward works in both jobs without changing shape.
normal.cn: 正因为那个后缀既能标形容词也能标副词，outward 不用改形就能兼任两职。

normal.en: British English adds -s for the adverb outwards, while American English usually keeps outward for both.
normal.cn: 英式英语给副词加 -s 写成 outwards，而美式英语通常两种用法都用 outward。

normal.en: An outward journey is the trip away from home; the trip back is the return journey.
normal.cn: an outward journey 是离家外出的那一段行程；回程则叫 the return journey。

normal.en: Outwardly adds -ly to mean on the surface, which is why an outwardly calm person may be far from calm.
normal.cn: outwardly 加 -ly 表示「表面上」，所以一个表面上镇定的人可能一点也不镇定。

abstract.en: A word about direction keeps reminding us that the same thing has an outside for other people and an inside for itself.
abstract.cn: 一个关于方向的词反复提醒人：同一件东西，对别人有外面，对自己有里面。

abstract.en: To be outward-looking is to turn the gaze away from one's own affairs, and the word makes that choice a direction rather than a virtue.
abstract.cn: 说一个人对外关注，就是把目光从自己的事务上移开，而这个词把这种选择说成一个方向，而不是一种美德。

abstract.en: Outward calm is not exactly a lie; it is the part of feeling that has been arranged for other people to see.
abstract.cn: 表面的平静并不完全是谎话；它只是感情里被整理好、供别人看的那一部分。

examples.en: The ship's outward journey took three days.
examples.cn: 这艘船出航用了三天。

examples.en: Outward calm hid a great deal of worry.
examples.cn: 表面的平静掩藏了大量忧虑。

examples.en: The doors open outward onto the courtyard.
examples.cn: 这些门向外开，通向院子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特沃德」——奥特转过身朝外面走；记住 outward 是向外的、外表的。

root: 由古英语 ūt（向外）加后缀 -weard（朝向）构成，古英语已写作 ūtweard；同族词有 inward、toward、homeward 等；-weard 属日耳曼语成分，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line drawn from inside to outside; the senses divide into direction, visible surface, dealings with the wider world, and the adverb of movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从内到外的一条线；义项按「方向」「可见的表面」「与外部世界的往来」「表示移动的副词」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat turned inside out, lining inwards, cloth facing the wind, the wind passing over that outer face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件外套被翻过来，里子朝内，布面朝外，风从那一面吹过去。

branches.en: a ship leaving the harbour at dawn
branches.cn: 清晨离港的一艘船

branches.en: a face that shows nothing of the worry
branches.cn: 不露忧虑的一张脸

branches.en: goods crossing a border towards buyers
branches.cn: 越过边境运往买主的货物

branches.en: a door swinging away from the room
branches.cn: 朝房间外推开的一扇门

branches.en: surface and direction share one form
branches.cn: 表面与方向共用一个形式

intro.en: The word is a direction adverb with an old suffix meaning turned towards, and English uses the single form for both adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是方向副词加上意为「朝向」的古老后缀，英语让同一个形式兼作形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Outward is built from Old English ūt and -weard, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this formation.
latinIntro.cn: outward 由古英语 ūt 与 -weard 构成，这一构词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 椭圆形的；卵形的；椭圆；椭圆形场地
definition_en: shaped like an egg, with no corners and two long sides, or a shape or a sports ground of that form
core_image: 一只白蛋放在木桌上，蛋壳的轮廓被晨光勾出一条柔和的线
scene: 旧货店的角落里放着一张矮桌，桌面被磨得发亮，四边没有一处直角。The table in the corner has an oval top.
sceneCN: 这里的 oval 是「椭圆形的」（第 1 个义项：像蛋一样的圆润形状）；句意为角落里那张桌子有一个椭圆形的桌面。图中可辨识物件：矮桌、磨亮的桌面、店角的阴影。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 ov-（蛋）加希腊来源的 -oid（像……的）构成，义为「卵形的」
来自拉丁语 ovatus（卵形的），多用于植物学，义为「卵形的」
由 oval 与 shaped 复合而成，义为「椭圆形的」

senses.title: Shaped like an egg
senses.definition: having a rounded shape that is longer than it is wide, with no corners, like an egg
senses.definitionCN: 圆润、长大于宽、没有棱角，形状像一枚蛋
senses.example: The table in the corner has an oval top.
senses.exampleCN: 角落里的那张桌子有一个椭圆形的桌面。
senses.why: Oval comes from the Latin word for an egg, so the shape is named after the most familiar object that has it.
senses.whyCN: oval 来自拉丁语中表示「蛋」的词，所以这个形状是用最常见、天生带着它的事物来命名的。

senses.title: A closed shape with two long sides
senses.definition: a flat shape with no corners, longer in one direction than in the other
senses.definitionCN: 一种没有棱角的平面形状，一个方向比另一个方向长
senses.example: She drew an oval on the board and divided it in two.
senses.exampleCN: 她在板上画了一个椭圆，把它分成两半。
senses.why: Once the adjective named the shape, English used the same word as a noun for the shape itself, without adding any suffix.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词已经命名了形状，英语就把同一个词直接作名词用，指形状本身，不必另加后缀。

senses.title: A ground or track of that shape
senses.definition: a sports ground or running track with an oval boundary, especially in cricket and Australian rules
senses.definitionCN: 边界呈椭圆形的运动场或跑道，尤用于板球与澳式足球
senses.example: The match was played on a small oval near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛在河边一个不大的椭圆场地上进行。
senses.why: A field bounded by that curve takes its name from the curve, which is why a cricket ground is simply called an oval.
senses.whyCN: 以这条曲线为边界的场地就借这条曲线得名，所以板球场干脆就叫「椭圆」。

intro.en: Oval comes from Latin ovum, an egg, through the adjective ovalis; English borrowed it from French in the seventeenth century and now uses it for the shape, the outline and the ground.
intro.cn: oval 来自拉丁语 ovum（蛋），经形容词 ovalis 而来；英语十七世纪从法语借入，如今用来指这种形状、这条轮廓以及这种场地。

items.en: Ovum was the ordinary Latin word for an egg, and it supplied the stem ov- for everything egg-shaped.
items.cn: ovum 是拉丁语中表示「蛋」的常用词，为一切与蛋形有关的事物提供了词干 ov-。

items.en: Ovatus meant egg-shaped, and Roman writers used it for anything with that kind of outline.
items.cn: ovatus 意为卵形的，罗马作家用它形容具有那种轮廓的东西。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed ovalis, an adjective built on ovum with the ending -alis, meaning belonging to.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出形容词 ovalis，由 ovum 加表示「属于……」的 -alis 构成。

items.en: French passed the adjective on as oval, and English adopted it in the seventeenth century for the curved outline itself.
items.cn: 法语把这一形容词作 oval 传出，英语在十七世纪借入，用来指这条弯曲的轮廓本身。

items.en: Modern English uses oval as an adjective, as a noun for the shape, and as a name for grounds bounded by that curve.
items.cn: 现代英语让 oval 兼作形容词、指形状的名词，以及以这条曲线为界的场地之名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin stem for egg; the near-meaning group collects words for rounded and elongated shapes.

normalIntro.en: Oval is an adjective grown from the Latin word for an egg, so its hooks go back to a kitchen object rather than to geometry.
normalIntro.cn: oval 是从拉丁语「蛋」长出来的形容词，所以记忆钩子回到一件厨房里的东西，而不是几何学。

normal.en: Oval starts from the Latin ovum, an egg, so the word literally means egg-shaped.
normal.cn: oval 从拉丁语 ovum（蛋）出发，字面上就是「蛋形的」。

normal.en: The same ov- stem gives ovary and ovum, which belong to the biology of eggs.
normal.cn: 同一个 ov- 词干还给出 ovary 与 ovum，都属于与卵有关的生物学。

normal.en: The famous office in the White House takes its name from the curved walls of that room, not from any egg.
normal.cn: 白宫那间著名的办公室得名于房间弯曲的墙，而不是因为任何一只蛋。

normal.en: Oval and circle differ in one point: an oval is stretched, so it has two long sides instead of one even radius.
normal.cn: oval 与 circle 只差一点：椭圆被拉长了，所以它有两条长边，而不是处处半径相等。

normal.en: The ending -al turns a Latin stem into an adjective, as it does in normal and final.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 把拉丁词干变成形容词，normal 与 final 也是如此。

abstract.en: A shape named after an egg suggests that geometry begins with things the hand already knows.
abstract.cn: 一个以蛋命名的形状说明：几何学是从手已经熟悉的东西开始的。

abstract.en: An oval has no corners, so it guides movement round instead of stopping it, which is why tracks are built in that shape.
abstract.cn: 椭圆没有棱角，所以它引导移动绕行而不是停下，跑道建成这个形状正是为此。

abstract.en: Naming a shape after the most ordinary object is a small admission that language grows out of the kitchen before it reaches the classroom.
abstract.cn: 用最平常的物件给形状命名，是承认语言先在厨房里长出来，之后才走进教室。

examples.en: The table in the corner has an oval top.
examples.cn: 角落里的那张桌子有一个椭圆形的桌面。

examples.en: She drew an oval on the board and divided it in two.
examples.cn: 她在板上画了一个椭圆，把它分成两半。

examples.en: The match was played on a small oval near the river.
examples.cn: 比赛在河边一个不大的椭圆场地上进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃」——欧沃手里捧着一只蛋，蛋的轮廓就是椭圆；记住 oval 是椭圆形的。

root: 来自中世纪拉丁语 ovalis（卵形的），再上溯拉丁语 ovum（蛋），十七世纪经法语进入英语；同族词多与「卵、蛋形」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the outline of an egg; the senses divide into the adjective for that shape, the noun for the curve itself, and the ground bounded by it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一枚蛋的轮廓；义项按「形容这种形状的形容词」「指这条曲线本身的名词」「以它为界的场地」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white egg on a wooden table, its outline traced by the morning light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白蛋放在木桌上，蛋壳的轮廓被晨光勾出一条柔和的线。

branches.en: a line chalked on a board and split in half
branches.cn: 在黑板上画出又被分成两半的一条线

branches.en: a field ringed by a low fence
branches.cn: 被一道矮栏围住的场地

branches.en: the shape in a table and the shape on a board
branches.cn: 桌面上的形状与板上的形状

branches.en: a curve that names both a figure and a field
branches.cn: 一条既命名图形又命名场地的曲线

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of belonging built on the noun for egg, passed through French and used in English for a shape, a figure and a ground.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在「蛋」这个名词上的拉丁语形容词，表示归属，经法语传入英语，用来指形状、图形与场地。

latinIntro.en: Latin ovum, ovatus and medieval Latin ovalis are all recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ovum、ovatus 与中世纪拉丁语 ovalis 均有记录，因此这一族词有可靠的拉丁语世系。

definition_zh: 烤箱；烤炉；灶；窑炉
definition_en: an enclosed chamber that is heated so that food can be baked inside it, and by extension any similar heated chamber used in industry or felt as unbearable heat
core_image: 玻璃门内一团橙光，铁架上的面团正慢慢鼓起
scene: 冬夜的厨房里，玻璃门内透出橙黄的光，铁架上的面团一点点鼓起来。He lifted the lid and a wave of heat rolled out of the oven.
sceneCN: 这里 oven 是「烤箱」（第 1 个义项：家里用来烘焙食物的封闭炉箱）；句意为他掀开盖子，一股热气从烤箱里滚出来，画面是玻璃门内那团橙光和鼓起来的面团。

derivatives.zh: 由 oven 与 -proof 复合而成，义为「耐烤箱高温的」
由 oven 与 -ware 复合而成，义为「烤箱用器皿」
由 oven 与 ready 复合而成，义为「可直接入炉烤制的」

senses.title: A heated box for baking food at home
senses.definition: an enclosed part of a cooker, heated by gas or electricity, in which food is baked or roasted
senses.definitionCN: 炉灶上用燃气或电加热的封闭部分，用来烘烤或烤制食物
senses.example: She slid the tray into the hot oven and set the timer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把烤盘推进滚烫的烤箱，定了时。
senses.why: Old English ofen named a heated clay chamber, so the core picture is a closed box holding heat rather than a machine; baking is simply what such a box was built to do.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ofen 指用火加热的泥土密室，所以这个词的底图是一只拢住热气的封闭箱子，而不是一台机器；烘焙只是这种箱子本来就承担的事，因此「烤箱」是最贴近底图的义项。

senses.title: The baking compartment of a cooker
senses.definition: the part of a kitchen stove that is closed off and heated for baking, as distinct from the burners on top
senses.definitionCN: 厨房炉灶上封闭加热、专门用于烘烤的部分，与上方的明火灶眼相对
senses.example: The casserole sat in the lower oven of the cooker.
senses.exampleCN: 炖锅放在炉灶下面那层烤室里。
senses.why: A cooker repeats the old chamber in miniature and puts it under the burners, so the word moves from a whole hearth to one compartment of a kitchen range.
senses.whyCN: 炉灶把旧式的加热室缩小后安在灶眼下面，于是这个词从整座火塘转到厨房灶具的一个隔间；词义缩小，指的还是那只装热气的箱子。

senses.title: An industrial chamber for firing or drying
senses.definition: a large heated chamber used in industry for firing clay, drying materials or turning coal into coke
senses.definitionCN: 工业上用的大型加热室，用于烧制陶土、烘干物料或把煤炼成焦炭
senses.example: A coke oven burns coal slowly to produce coke for steel making.
senses.exampleCN: 炼焦炉把煤慢慢加热，为炼钢生产焦炭。
senses.why: Brick ovens and coke ovens enlarge the same chamber and trap heat around clay or coal instead of dough, so the name follows the shape of the box rather than the food inside.
senses.whyCN: 砖窑与炼焦炉把同一只加热室放大，把热气拢在陶土或煤的周围而不是面团周围；名字跟着箱子的形状走，不跟着里面的东西走，于是义项从厨房扩到工厂。

senses.title: A room or place that feels unbearably hot
senses.definition: a room or enclosed space that is so hot and airless that it feels like the inside of an oven
senses.definitionCN: 热而不透风的房间或封闭空间，待在里面像待在烤箱里一样
senses.example: The attic was an oven by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到了中午，阁楼热得像烤箱。
senses.why: The comparison works by sensation rather than by cooking: a person standing in a closed hot room feels the same blast that comes out when an oven door opens, so the word crosses over to discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻靠的是体感而不是烹饪：人站在不透风的闷热房间里，感到的正是烤箱门打开时扑出的那股热浪，所以这个词跨到「难受的闷热」这一边。

intro.en: Oven is an inherited Germanic word for a heated chamber, and its recorded history in English reaches back to the first written texts.
intro.cn: oven 是日耳曼语中表示「加热密室」的固有词，它在英语里的记录可以上溯到最早的文献。

items.en: A form usually reconstructed as ufnaz or uhnaz gave the Germanic languages their word for a baking chamber, though the exact shape of the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般把日耳曼语的这个词重构为 ufnaz 或 uhnaz，意为烘焙用的加热室，但重构的确切形式仍有争议。

items.en: Old English ofen named a dome-shaped chamber of clay or stone with a fire lit inside it.
items.cn: 古英语 ofen 指圆顶的泥土或石头加热室，火就生在室内。

items.en: Middle English kept both the sense and the spelling, and a village often shared one large oven for the whole week's bread.
items.cn: 中古英语保留原义与原拼写，一个村子常常共用一座大炉烤一整周的面包。

items.en: Iron ranges brought a smaller oven indoors beside the fire, and the word settled into the kitchen.
items.cn: 铁炉灶把较小的烤室搬进室内、安在火边，这个词就此落进厨房。

items.en: Gas, electric and microwave ovens still name the same closed chamber, while a sweltering room is also called an oven.
items.cn: 燃气炉、电烤箱与微波炉沿用的仍是那只封闭加热室，而闷热的房间也被叫作 oven。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built directly on the noun; the near-meaning group collects other chambers and appliances that produce or hold heat.
note.cn: 形近组收直接由这个名词构成的复合词；近义组收其他产生热量或拢住热量的炉具与炉室。

entries.definition: Made to withstand the heat inside an oven without cracking.
entries.definitionCN: 经得起烤箱内的高温而不裂的。

entries.definition: Dishes and pans designed for use inside an oven.
entries.definitionCN: 专为在烤箱内使用而做的盘碟与烤盘。

entries.definition: Prepared and packed so that it can go straight into an oven.
entries.definitionCN: 已备好包装、可直接送进烤箱的。

entries.definition: Cooked by dry heat inside an oven rather than on a hob.
entries.definitionCN: 在烤箱内用干热烤熟，而不是在灶眼上煎煮。

entries.definition: An appliance with burners on top and often an oven below.
entries.definitionCN: 上方有灶眼、下方常带烤室的炉具。

entries.definition: A very hot enclosed space used to heat a building or melt materials.
entries.definitionCN: 用于供暖或熔炼材料的高温封闭炉。

entries.definition: A chamber for firing pottery, bricks or lime at high temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 用于高温烧制陶器、砖或石灰的窑。

entries.definition: An appliance that heats food with electromagnetic waves instead of a flame.
entries.definitionCN: 用电磁波而非明火加热食物的炉具。

normalIntro.en: The word names a box that holds heat, and its hooks return to the chamber, its fuel and the compounds built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词说的是「拢住热气的箱子」，记忆钩子都回到那间加热室、它的燃料，以及由它构成的复合词。

normal.en: Old English ofen and German Ofen are cousins, so the word has meant a heated chamber for more than a thousand years.
normal.cn: 古英语 ofen 与德语 Ofen 是同源词，所以这个词指加热室已有一千多年。

normal.en: The noun names the box, not the fuel, which is why wood, gas and electric versions all keep one name.
normal.cn: 这个名词命名的是箱子而不是燃料，所以柴火、燃气与电热的版本共用一个名字。

normal.en: Ovenproof adds a suffix meaning resistant, so the word describes what the heat cannot do to the dish.
normal.cn: ovenproof 加上表示「抗得住」的后缀，说的是高温拿这只盘子没办法。

normal.en: Microwave oven puts the new heating method in front of the old noun instead of inventing a fresh word.
normal.cn: microwave oven 把新的加热方式摆在旧名词前面，而没有另造新词。

normal.en: A room called an oven borrows only the heat of the box, not its shape or its purpose.
normal.cn: 被叫作 oven 的房间只借了箱子的热度，不借它的形状与用途。

abstract.en: A glass door glowing orange in a dark kitchen is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 暗厨房里一扇透出橙光的玻璃门，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A baker drawing a long wooden peel out of a brick mouth shows the word before it entered the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 面包师从砖砌炉口抽出长木铲，显示这个词走进厨房之前的样子。

abstract.en: A closed attic at noon shows the word sliding from cooking to plain discomfort.
abstract.cn: 正午紧闭的阁楼，显示这个词从烹饪滑向单纯的难受。

examples.en: She slid the tray into the hot oven and set the timer.
examples.cn: 她把烤盘推进滚烫的烤箱，定了时。

examples.en: The village still bakes its bread in a wood-fired oven.
examples.cn: 村里仍用柴火烤炉烤面包。

examples.cn: 到了中午，阁楼热得像烤箱。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a closed chamber that holds heat; the senses move from the kitchen box to the cooker compartment, then to the industrial kiln, and finally to a room that feels like one.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一只拢住热气的封闭箱室；义项从厨房里的烤箱，转到炉灶上的烤室，再转到工业窑炉，最后转到热得像炉子的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: orange light behind a glass door, a tray of dough rising slowly on an iron rack.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃门后透出橙光，铁架上一盘面团正慢慢鼓起。

branches.cn: 砖窑向夜色里吐着热气

branches.cn: 正午关着窗的阁楼

branches.en: one trapped heat, once welcomed and once endured
branches.cn: 同一种拢住的热，一次被欢迎，一次被忍受

latinIntro.en: This is a Germanic word with no reliable Latin cognate; Latin terms for a stove or furnace belong to other families.

senses.title: Above and across something

senses.definitionCN: 高于并跨过某物

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the word's real partners: its fixed phrase, its family, its recorded origin and its closest field.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子都建立在真实材料上：固定搭配、词族、可查的词源与最近的语义场。

normal.en: The fixed phrase 'over the bridge' gives the word one clear home.
normal.cn: 固定搭配「over the bridge」给了这个词一个清楚的落点。

normal.en: The family word 'overly' shows how the meaning extends.
normal.cn: 词族里的「overly」展示了词义如何向外延伸。

normal.en: Its recorded origin passes through OLD ENGLISH OFER and ABOVE AND ACROSS.
normal.cn: 可查的来源经过 OLD ENGLISH OFER 与 ABOVE AND ACROSS 两个阶段。

normal.en: In the same field sits 'above'; compare the two when you recall the word.
normal.cn: 同一语义场里还有「above」，回想时把两者放在一起比较。

normal.en: The form 'over' is what you will meet in running text.
normal.cn: 在连续文本里，你常遇到的形式是「over」。

abstract.en: Picture a child flying a kite above his head, the string passing over the treetops, then let the picture change size until it covers both the everyday object and the figurative use.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子把风筝放过头顶，线越过树梢，再让画面变大变小，直到它同时罩住日常实物与比喻用法。

abstract.en: Place the word inside the scene given in this entry; what stays in memory is the picture, not the translation.
abstract.cn: 把 over 放进本词条给出的场景里；留在记忆里的是画面，不是翻译。

definition_en: including everything; considered as a whole; in general; (overalls) a protective garment worn over other clothes
core_image: 从高处俯视整张地图，所有街道一次收进眼里

sceneCN: 这里 overall 是“总体的、把一切算在内的”（第 1 个义项：包括全部）；句意：她的总体判断很简单：项目略慢，但质量与预算都在可控范围内。图中可辨识物件：项目看板、进度曲线、预算表、会议桌；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Including everything
senses.definition: covering or including all parts, without leaving anything out
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖或包括所有部分，不遗漏任何一项
senses.example: The overall cost of the project was higher than planned.
senses.exampleCN: 项目的总成本高于计划。
senses.why: Overall began as over + all, 'everywhere, in every part'. The modern 1894 sense 'taking all into consideration' keeps the same picture: the word spreads over the whole instead of standing inside one part.
senses.whyCN: overall 原为 over + all，意为“到处、在每个部分”。1894 年的现代义“把一切考虑在内”保留同一画面：这个词铺在整个整体之上，而不是站在某一部分里。

senses.title: The total amount
senses.definition: the combined amount after all parts have been added together
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分相加后的合计量
senses.example: Overall spending rose by six percent.
senses.exampleCN: 总支出上升了百分之六。
senses.why: Once the word covers all parts, it can name their sum. The movement is from spatial coverage to arithmetic total: everything is gathered under one figure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词覆盖所有部分，它就能命名它们的总和。意义从空间覆盖转到算术合计：一切被收拢到一个数字之下。

senses.title: A general impression
senses.definition: a judgment based on the whole rather than on separate details
senses.definitionCN: 基于整体而非各个细节作出的判断
senses.example: My overall impression was of a well-run school.
senses.exampleCN: 我的总体印象是这是一所管理良好的学校。
senses.why: An impression formed 'over all' is built by stepping back from details. The word marks the level at which separate observations merge into one feeling.
senses.whyCN: “覆盖全部”形成的印象，是从细节退后一步得到的。这个词标记的是各个观察合并成一种感受的那个层级。

senses.title: The whole picture
senses.definition: the complete situation seen as one connected picture
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个相互关联的整体来看的完整局面
senses.example: The report gives an overall picture of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告给出了该地区的整体图景。
senses.why: The metaphor is visual: an observer moves above the parts and sees how they fit. Overall names that altitude of view, not the individual objects below.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻是视觉性的：观察者升到各部分之上，看见它们如何拼合。overall 命名的是这个观察高度，而不是下方的单个物体。

senses.title: Generally speaking
senses.definition: used to sum up a judgment after weighing the details
senses.definitionCN: 在权衡细节之后用来概括判断
senses.example: Overall, the experiment succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 总体来说，实验是成功的。
senses.why: As an adverb, the word performs the summing-up act itself. It tells the listener that the sentence to follow is a verdict after the parts have been counted, not another detail.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时，这个词本身就在做“汇总”这个动作。它告诉听者：接下来的句子是清点完各部分后的裁决，而不是又一条细节。

senses.title: Overalls: a garment worn over all
senses.titleCN: 工装裤：穿在其他衣服外面的衣物
senses.definition: a protective garment, usually trousers with a bib, worn over ordinary clothes
senses.definitionCN: 穿在日常衣服外面的防护衣物，通常是有胸兜的裤子
senses.example: The mechanic wiped his hands on his overalls.
senses.exampleCN: 机修工在工装裤上擦了擦手。
senses.why: The noun overalls uses the literal spatial sense: a garment worn over all the other clothes. The same 'covering everything' idea that governs the adjective is here made of cloth.
senses.whyCN: 名词 overalls 用的是字面空间义：穿在所有其他衣服外面的衣物。支配形容词的“覆盖全部”观念，在这里是用布做成的。

senses.title: Combined-score champion
senses.definition: the winner judged on the total of all events rather than a single one
senses.definitionCN: 按所有项目的总和而非单项评出的优胜者
senses.example: She took the overall title by two points.
senses.exampleCN: 她以两分之差拿下总冠军。
senses.why: In sport, overall marks the level at which separate events are added into one standing. The word directs attention away from any single race and toward the whole series.
senses.whyCN: 在体育中，overall 标记的是把各单项加总成一个总排名的层级。这个词把注意力从任何一场比赛移开，转向整个系列赛。

senses.title: Whole-system responsibility
senses.definition: responsibility for the whole of an operation rather than one part of it
senses.definitionCN: 对整个运作而非某一部分负责
senses.example: He has overall responsibility for safety.
senses.exampleCN: 他对安全负总责。
senses.why: This use turns the spatial word into an organizational one: a person stands above all the parts and answers for how they work together. Coverage becomes accountability.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法把空间词变成组织词：一个人站在所有部分之上，对它们如何协同负责。覆盖变成了问责。

intro.en: Overall is native English, built from over and all. Its oldest sense was 'everywhere'; the modern 'all things considered' is only from 1894.
intro.cn: overall 是英语本族词，由 over 与 all 构成。最古老的义项是“到处”；现代“把所有事都考虑在内”的义项直到 1894 年才出现。

items.en: The phrase ofer eall meant 'everywhere, in every part or place'. The modern spelling overall comes from Middle English over-al.
items.cn: 短语 ofer eall 意为“到处、在每个部分或地方”。现代拼写 overall 来自中世纪英语 over-al。

items.en: Over-al kept the sense 'everywhere'. That original sense is now obsolete in standard English.
items.cn: over-al 保留“到处”之义。这个原始义项在现代标准英语中已废弃。

items.en: The modern meaning 'including everything, taking all into consideration' is recorded.
items.cn: 现代义“包括一切、把全部考虑在内”被记录。

items.en: The garment sense of overalls (trousers worn over other clothes) belongs to the same literal idea of something worn over all.
items.cn: overalls（穿在其他衣服外面的裤子）的衣物义，同属“穿在所有东西外面”这一字面观念。具体年代各家说法不一，此处只取通行理解。

items.en: The word now works as adjective, adverb, and noun. Its unity is the idea of a view or covering that spans every part.
items.cn: 这个词现在是形容词、副词和名词。它的统一性在于一个横跨每个部分的视角或覆盖。

note.cn: 形近组区分其他 over- 复合词；近义组按“包含多少”来区分。

entries.definition: covering the main features rather than details. It stresses breadth of scope, not the act of summing up.

entries.definition: including nearly all relevant items. It is stronger and more formal than overall and usually implies a deliberate completeness.
entries.definitionCN: 包括几乎所有相关项目。它比 overall 更强、更正式，通常暗示刻意的完整。

entries.definition: considering everything; generally. It is the adverbial phrase closest to overall in its summing-up use.
entries.definitionCN: 总的来说；大体上。它是最接近 overall 汇总用法的副词短语。

normal.en: An overall winner is not the winner of one race but of the whole series.

abstract.en: To see overall is to change altitude: details do not disappear, they become pattern.
abstract.cn: 看“整体”就是换高度：细节没有消失，而是变成了图案。

abstract.en: Every whole is a decision about which parts to count and which to leave outside the frame.
abstract.cn: 每个“整体”都是一次决定：哪些部分算进来，哪些留在画框之外。

abstract.en: Overall judgment is what remains after the numbers stop arguing with each other.

definition_zh: 克服；战胜；压倒；使受不了
definition_en: to deal successfully with a difficulty, to defeat an opponent, or to make someone helpless with a strong feeling or with fumes and heat
core_image: 一个人顶着风爬到最后一道坡顶，身后是散开的队伍
scene: 山口的雪还没化，队伍里有人喘得说不出话，领队回头指了指前面那道坡。The team overcame the last steep section just before dark.
sceneCN: 这里 overcame 是「克服」（第 1 个义项：把困难顶过去）；句意为队伍在天黑前越过了最后一段陡坡，画面是山口残雪与喘着气的人。

pos.zh: 克服；战胜；压倒；使受不了

derivatives.zh: 由 overcome 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「克服者；战胜者」
由 overcome 加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「克服；战胜的过程」

senses.title: To deal successfully with a difficulty
senses.definition: to succeed in dealing with a problem, obstacle or difficult condition that stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 成功处理挡在面前的难题、障碍或艰难处境
senses.example: She had to overcome her fear of heights before she could cross the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她得先克服恐高，才敢走过那座桥。
senses.why: The oldest form of the verb is over plus come, meaning to arrive on top of something; a difficulty is treated as ground a person has to get across, so success is pictured as reaching the other side.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最早是 over 加 come，意为「来到某物之上」；困难被当成一片必须走过去的土地，所以「克服」在画面上就是走到了对面。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent
senses.definition: to get the better of an enemy or rival in a contest, fight or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在竞赛、打斗或争论中压过对手或敌手
senses.example: He overcame his opponent in three straight sets.
senses.exampleCN: 他连下三盘战胜了对手。
senses.why: If coming over something can mean standing on top of it, the same movement serves for a rival: the winner is the one left standing over the other, and the sporting sense follows.
senses.whyCN: 既然「来到某物之上」可以指站到它上面，同一个动作也能用在对手身上：赢家是最后站着、把对方压在下面的那个人，竞技义就由此而来。

senses.title: To make someone helpless with feeling or fumes
senses.definition: usually in the passive, to affect someone so strongly with emotion, heat or fumes that they lose control of themselves
senses.definitionCN: 常用于被动式，指被情绪、热气或烟味冲击到失去自持
senses.example: She was overcome with relief when the results arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 结果传来时，她松了一口气，几乎站不住。
senses.why: A person who is overcome has been come over by something heavier than a task; the same verb that marks getting on top of a problem marks a feeling getting on top of the person.
senses.whyCN: 被 overcome 的人，是被某种比任务更沉的东西压在上面；同一个动词既表示人爬到问题之上，也表示情绪爬到人之上，被动式于是有了「被压倒」的一面。

senses.title: To come upon suddenly, as in older usage
senses.definition: in older writing, to come upon someone or something suddenly, without the modern idea of winning
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文字里指突然来到某人或某物身上，不含现代「取胜」的意思
senses.example: A great weariness overcame the travellers at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时，一阵极度的疲惫袭向这些旅人。
senses.why: This is the literal layer that the other senses grew from: over as arrival upon a place, with no struggle yet implied, preserved in a few literary phrases.
senses.whyCN: 这是其余义项生长出来的字面层：over 表示「来到某处之上」，此时还没有争胜的意味，只在少数书面说法里保留下来。

intro.en: Overcome was made inside English from two inherited words, and its history runs from plain arrival to victory and then to being flattened by feeling.
intro.cn: overcome 由两个英语固有词在英语内部合成，词义从「到达」走到「取胜」，再走到「被情绪压垮」。

items.en: Over and come both descend from reconstructed Germanic forms, so the compound belongs to the inherited vocabulary rather than to borrowed Latin.
items.cn: over 与 come 都上溯到重构的日耳曼语形式，所以这个复合词属于固有词汇，不是从拉丁语借来的。

items.en: Old English ofercuman meant to come upon a person or place, and from that contact it also meant to get the better of someone.
items.cn: 古英语 ofercuman 指来到某人或某地之上，又从这种接触引申出压过对方的意思。

items.en: Middle English pushed the verb toward victory in battle and success against an obstacle, while the plain arrival sense faded.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个动词推向战场上的胜利与对障碍的克服，单纯的「到达」义则淡出。

items.en: The passive pattern be overcome with gave the word a new task, describing a person flattened by grief, heat or fumes.
items.cn: 被动结构 be overcome with 给了这个词新任务，用来描述被悲伤、热气或烟味压垮的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the active sense of mastering a problem and the passive sense of being overwhelmed, plus an archaic use for coming upon.
items.cn: 现代英语保留主动的「解决问题」与被动的「被压倒」，另有一层古旧的「突然降临」用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same verb and other compounds built with over; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of winning and of being overwhelmed.

entries.definition: The present participle, used for the process still going on.

entries.definition: To put too much weight or too many demands on something.

entries.definition: To take control of a place or people by force.

entries.definition: To beat someone in a battle, game or election.
entries.definitionCN: 在战斗、比赛或选举中击败某人。

entries.definition: To deal successfully with a difficulty or obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 成功处理困难或障碍。

entries.definition: To affect someone so strongly that they cannot think or act.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈影响某人，使其无法思考或行动。

normalIntro.en: The word is over plus come, and its hooks return to that arrival, to the fight, and to the feeling that arrives on top of a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 over 加 come，记忆钩子都回到那次「到达」、那场争斗，以及压到人头上的情绪。

normal.en: Over and come are both native Germanic words, so overcome was assembled in English rather than borrowed whole.
normal.cn: over 与 come 都是日耳曼语固有词，所以 overcome 是在英语里拼起来的，不是整体借入的。

normal.en: The oldest sense is arrival, which is why an old sentence can say that weariness overcame someone without any fight.
normal.cn: 最老的一层意思是「到达」，所以旧句里可以说疲惫袭向某人，而不含争斗。

normal.en: Victory is pictured as standing over the other person, and that picture produced the modern sense of defeating.
normal.cn: 胜利被画成站在对方之上，这幅画产出了现代的「击败」义。

normal.en: The passive be overcome with keeps the same downward pressure: the feeling is now the thing on top.
normal.cn: 被动式 be overcome with 保留了同一股向下的压力，只是这回压在上面的是情绪。

normal.en: Overdo and overload share the prefix but not the victory, which shows how far over can stretch.
normal.cn: overdo 与 overload 共用前缀却没有胜负之意，可见 over 能拉得多远。

abstract.en: A climber topping the last ridge with the wind at his back is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 登山者顶着风翻过最后一道山脊，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A wrestler left standing over his rival turns arrival into victory.
abstract.cn: 摔跤手站在对手之上，把「到达」变成了「取胜」。

abstract.en: A letter read at the door, hand shaking, shows how a feeling can arrive on top of a person.
abstract.cn: 在门口读信、手发抖，说明一种情绪如何压到人身上。

examples.en: She had to overcome her fear of heights before she could cross the bridge.
examples.cn: 她得先克服恐高，才敢走过那座桥。

examples.en: He overcame his opponent in three straight sets.
examples.cn: 他连下三盘战胜了对手。

examples.en: She was overcome with relief when the results arrived.
examples.cn: 结果传来时，她松了一口气，几乎站不住。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arriving on top of something; the senses run from crossing a difficulty, to standing over a rival, to a feeling standing over the person, and back to the old literal arrival.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「来到某物之上」；义项从越过困难，到站到对手之上，到情绪压到人头上，再回到古老的「突然降临」。

branches.cn: 登山者硬撑着爬上最后一段坡

branches.cn: 摔跤手站在对手之上

branches.cn: 手抖着读信的人

branches.cn: 同一种压力，一次被顶回去，一次被承受

intro.en: The word joins the Old English prefix for over with the verb to come, then feeds a small family of forms and other over- compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在上」的前缀与动词「来」连在一起，再由它生出几个形式与别的 over 复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is a Germanic compound with no Latin family of its own; Latin super is only a distant relative of the prefix over, not a member of this word's family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语复合词，本身没有拉丁词族；拉丁语 super 只是前缀 over 的远亲，不算这个词族的成员。

sceneCN: 这里 overhead 是「在头顶上方」（第 1 个义项：副词，位置在头顶之上）；句意为一架飞机从头顶飞过，盖住了人行道上的谈话，画面是老街上方的电车线网。

senses.title: Above a person's head
senses.titleCN: 在头顶上方；在空中（副词）
senses.definition: in the air directly above someone, without touching the ground or any surface
senses.definitionCN: 在空中正对某人头顶的位置，不接触地面或任何表面
senses.example: A fan hummed overhead while we waited in the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在走廊里等着，头顶上一台风扇嗡嗡地转。
senses.why: The compound is over plus head, so the first sense simply puts a thing on the far side of the head; no metaphor is involved yet.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词就是 over 加 head，所以第一个义项只是把东西放到头顶的另一侧；此时还没有任何比喻。

senses.title: Fixed or passing above the ground
senses.titleCN: 头顶上的；架空的（形容词）
senses.definition: placed high enough to clear people and traffic, as wires, railways or beams
senses.definitionCN: 架得足够高，能让开行人与车辆，如电线、铁路或横梁
senses.example: The village still gets its power from overhead cables.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子仍靠架空电缆供电。
senses.why: Once the word marks the space above the head, anything built to occupy that space takes the same label, so the adverb becomes an adjective describing structures.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出头顶那片空间，任何被造来占用那片空间的东西都能带上它，于是副词变形容词，用来形容构筑物。

senses.title: The regular costs of running a business
senses.definition: the fixed costs of running a business, such as rent, lighting and administration, that are not tied to one product
senses.definitionCN: 企业运转的固定成本，如房租、照明与行政开支，不直接计入某一件产品
senses.example: The company cut its overheads by moving to a smaller office.
senses.exampleCN: 公司搬到更小的办公室，压低了经常开支。
senses.why: In bookkeeping these costs sit above the individual jobs the way a ceiling sits above a room: they must be paid whatever is produced, so the word for what is above the head becomes the word for costs that hang over the whole business.
senses.whyCN: 在账目里，这些成本像天花板一样悬在每一项具体工作之上：不管生产什么都得付，于是「头顶之上」的词变成了悬在整个生意上方的开销。

senses.title: A stroke hit down from above
senses.definition: in tennis, squash or badminton, a stroke played with the racket raised above the head and swung downwards
senses.definitionCN: 网球、壁球或羽毛球中，把球拍举过头顶向下击出的球
senses.example: He finished the point with a powerful overhead smash.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记有力的过顶扣杀拿下这一分。
senses.why: The sporting sense keeps the physical picture without any transfer: the racket really does travel above the head, so the same word names the shot by the place it is played.
senses.whyCN: 运动义没有转移，只是照搬了身体画面：球拍确实从头顶上方挥过，于是同一个词按击球的位置给这一拍命名。

intro.en: Overhead is an English compound of two inherited words, first a phrase for position and later a label for wires, railways and business costs.
intro.cn: overhead 是由两个英语固有词构成的复合词，先是表示位置的短语，后来用来标注电线、铁路与经营成本。

items.en: Over and head both descend from reconstructed Germanic forms, so the compound was put together inside English's own vocabulary.
items.cn: over 与 head 都上溯到重构的日耳曼语形式，所以这个复合词是在英语自身词汇里拼合的。

items.en: Old English wrote ofer heafod as two words for something passing above a person's head.
items.cn: 古英语把 ofer heafod 写成两个词，指从头顶上方经过的东西。

items.en: Middle English kept the phrase for position and began to apply it to beams and roofs lying above a room.
items.cn: 中古英语保留这个表示位置的短语，并开始用它指横在房间上方的梁与顶。

items.en: Railways and telegraph wires made an adjective useful, and businesses began to speak of overhead as the cost of simply keeping the doors open.
items.cn: 铁路与电报线让形容词用法有了用处，商家开始用 overhead 指仅仅维持开门营业所需的花费。

items.en: Modern English uses the adverb for position, the plural nouns for fixed costs, and a singular noun for a stroke struck downwards.
items.cn: 现代英语用副词表示位置，用复数名词表示固定开支，又用单数名词指自上而下击出的球。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the plural noun and the compounds built with this word; the near-meaning group gathers words of position above and words for business costs.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复数名词以及由它构成的复合词；近义组收表示「上方位置」与表示「经营成本」的词。

entries.definition: The amounts of money that must be paid to run or produce something.
entries.definitionCN: 为运转或生产某物必须支付的金额。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply over plus head, and its hooks return to that height, to the structures that occupy it, and to the costs that hang over a business.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 over 加 head，记忆钩子都回到那个高度、占用那个高度的构筑物，以及悬在生意上方的成本。

normal.en: Overhead is over plus head, so anything placed or moving above the head can take the word.
normal.cn: overhead 是 over 加 head，凡是放在头顶上方或从头顶移过的东西都能用它。

normal.en: The adverb came first and the adjective followed, which is why wires and railways are described with the same word.
normal.cn: 先有副词，后有形容词，所以电线与铁路也用同一个词来形容。

normal.en: Overheads are called that because the rent and the lighting hang over every job like a ceiling.
normal.cn: 经常开支得名，是因为房租与照明像天花板一样悬在每一项工作之上。

normal.en: The final s matters: overheads in the plural is the business sense, while an overhead in sport is one stroke.
normal.cn: 末尾的 s 很关键：复数 overheads 是经营开支，运动里的 an overhead 则是一记球。

normal.en: An overhead smash keeps the literal picture, since the racket really passes above the head.
normal.cn: 过顶扣杀保留了字面画面，因为球拍确实从头顶上方挥过。

abstract.en: A tram wire drawn across a summer street is the word as pure position.
abstract.cn: 夏天街道上方拉过的一条电车线，就是这个词作为纯粹位置的样子。

abstract.en: A ceiling with lamps hanging from it turns height into a bill somebody has to pay.
abstract.cn: 挂着灯的天花板，把高度变成了一张总得有人付的账单。

abstract.en: A raised arm coming down on a ball shows the same word at the moment it becomes an action.

examples.en: The company cut its overheads by moving to a smaller office.
examples.cn: 公司搬到更小的办公室，压低了经常开支。

examples.en: He finished the point with a powerful overhead smash.
examples.cn: 他用一记有力的过顶扣杀拿下这一分。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the space above the head; the senses move from position, to structures that occupy it, to costs that hang over a business, and to a stroke struck from above.

definition_zh: 忽略；未注意；俯瞰；宽容；监督
definition_en: to fail to notice something, to have a view over a place from above, to forgive a fault, or in older use to watch over work or people
core_image: 山腰旅店朝西的窗，窗下是一片屋瓦和几条窄巷
scene: 山腰的旅店有一扇朝西的窗，窗下是一片屋瓦和几条窄巷。From the terrace you can overlook the whole harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 overlook 是「俯瞰」（第 2 个义项：从高处望下去）；句意为从平台上可以把整个港口尽收眼底，画面是那扇朝西的窗与窗下的屋瓦。

pos.zh: 忽略；未注意；俯瞰；宽容；监督

derivatives.zh: 由 overlook 加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成，义为「被忽略的」
由 overlook 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「监工；监督者」，多见于旧时纺织业记载

senses.title: To fail to notice something
senses.definition: to fail to see or consider something important, usually without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 没能看到或考虑到重要的事，通常并非有意
senses.example: The report overlooks one important detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告漏掉了一个重要细节。
senses.why: The verb pictures an eye sweeping over a surface; whatever the sweep passes across without stopping is literally looked over, and that is the root of the modern sense of missing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词画的是目光扫过一整片表面；凡是目光扫过却没有停下的地方，就是字面地被「看过而越过」，现代「漏看」义正由此而来。

senses.title: To have a view over a place from above
senses.definition: to be built or placed high enough to give a view down onto a place
senses.definitionCN: 建得或放得足够高，可以从上面望见某处
senses.example: Her office overlooks the river.
senses.exampleCN: 她的办公室可以俯瞰那条河。
senses.why: Here the eye really does travel over the whole scene from a height, so the word keeps its oldest physical meaning instead of turning it into a mistake.
senses.whyCN: 这里目光确实从高处扫过整片景物，所以这个词保留着最古老的身体经验，没有把它变成一种过失。

senses.title: To forgive a fault
senses.definition: to choose not to punish or complain about a fault, as if deciding not to see it
senses.definitionCN: 选择不处罚、不追究某个过失，好像决定不去看它
senses.example: The manager decided to overlook the late arrival.
senses.exampleCN: 经理决定不计较那次迟到。
senses.why: Forgiving is pictured as letting the eye pass over a fault without stopping on it; the same sweep that causes a genuine miss becomes, by choice, an act of leniency.
senses.whyCN: 宽恕被画成让目光从过失上滑过、不停留；同一次「扫过」，无意时是漏看，存心时就成了宽待。

senses.title: To watch over work or people
senses.definition: in older use, to keep an eye on workers or a process and make sure things are done properly
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法里指盯着工人或某道工序，确保事情做得妥当
senses.example: An old woman overlooked the girls at their sewing.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老妇人照看着这些姑娘做针线。
senses.why: A person standing above a workshop sees every bench at once, so the word for a wide view also served for supervision before oversee took over that job.
senses.whyCN: 站在作坊高处的人能一眼看见每张工作台，所以表示「放眼望全」的词也承担过监督之职，后来这份差事才交给 oversee。

intro.en: Overlook is an English compound of over and look; its story is the double edge of a gaze that sweeps across everything and therefore may stop on nothing.
intro.cn: overlook 是 over 与 look 的英语复合词，它的来历是一道目光的两面：既扫过全部，也可能什么都不停留。

items.en: Over and look are both inherited Germanic words, so the compound was formed in English rather than borrowed from French or Latin.
items.cn: over 与 look 都是日耳曼语固有词，所以这个复合词形成于英语内部，并非借自法语或拉丁语。

items.en: The recorded verb oferlocian meant to look over something, with the eye passing across a whole surface.
items.cn: 有记录的动词 oferlocian 意为「看过某物」，目光扫过整片表面。

items.en: Middle English overlooken kept the wide view and also began to mean passing over a thing without stopping on it.
items.cn: 中古英语 overlooken 保留「放眼望过」，也开始表示从某物上掠过而不再停留。

items.en: Two seemingly opposite senses grew from the same sweep of the eye: watching over a place, and letting a fault go by.
items.cn: 两个看似相反的义项从同一次扫视里长出来：一个是看住一处地方，一个是把过失放过去。

items.en: Modern English keeps the view from above, the failure to notice and the mild forgiveness, while the supervising sense has grown rare.
items.cn: 现代英语保留从高处望下去、漏看与轻微宽容三个义项，监督义则已少见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflected forms and other words built with the same prefix; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of ignoring, of viewing and of forgiving.
note.cn: 形近组收各种屈折形式与同一前缀构成的其他词；近义组收表示忽略、观看与宽恕的动词。

entries.definition: The past form, also used as an adjective for something not noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，也作形容词指未被注意的。

entries.definition: The present participle, often used of a building with a view.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，常用于描述有景可望的建筑。

entries.definition: To supervise work or people and make sure it is done properly.
entries.definitionCN: 监督管理或人员，确保事情做得妥当。

entries.definition: A failure to notice something, or the act of supervising.
entries.definitionCN: 未注意到某事，或监督这件事本身。

entries.definition: To pay no attention to something on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 故意不去理会某事。

entries.definition: To fail to give proper care or attention to something.
entries.definitionCN: 未能给予应有的照料或注意。

entries.definition: To stop being angry with someone for a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 因某个过失而不再生某人的气。

entries.definition: To look carefully over a whole area or scene.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细察看一整片区域或景象。

normalIntro.en: The word is over plus look, and its hooks return to a gaze that covers everything, to the height it needs, and to what it chooses not to see.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 over 加 look，记忆钩子都回到那道覆盖一切的目光、它需要的高度，以及它选择不看的东西。

normal.en: Overlook is over plus look, so the eye is pictured moving across a surface rather than fixing on a point.
normal.cn: overlook 是 over 加 look，画面里目光扫过一整片表面，而不是停在一点上。

normal.en: A building that overlooks the sea really does have that view, which is why the oldest sense survives unchanged.
normal.cn: 俯瞰大海的房子确实有那片景，所以最老的义项原样活了下来。

normal.en: The same sweep explains the mistake: what the eye passes over is not registered.
normal.cn: 同一次扫视也解释了过失：目光掠过的东西没有被记下。

normal.en: Forgiving adds a choice to the same picture, since the fault is deliberately allowed to pass.
normal.cn: 宽恕在同一幅画上加了选择：过失被故意放了过去。

normal.en: Oversee and oversight show that supervision once shared this prefix's wide view.
normal.cn: oversee 与 oversight 说明监督原本也共享这个前缀的「放眼望全」。

abstract.en: A window above a harbour with roofs and alleys below is the word as pure view.
abstract.cn: 港口上方的窗，下面是屋瓦与窄巷，就是这个词作为纯粹视野的样子。

abstract.en: A clerk running a finger down a list and skipping a line shows how a view becomes an error.
abstract.cn: 职员手指顺着名单下滑、跳过一行，显示视野如何变成错误。

abstract.en: A manager closing a file without a word turns the same skipped line into mercy.
abstract.cn: 经理一言不发合上卷宗，把同一行被跳过的地方变成了宽容。

examples.en: The report overlooks one important detail.
examples.cn: 这份报告漏掉了一个重要细节。

examples.en: Her office overlooks the river.
examples.cn: 她的办公室可以俯瞰那条河。

examples.en: The manager decided to overlook the late arrival.
examples.cn: 经理决定不计较那次迟到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃路克」——欧沃站在高处往下看，看得远，也容易漏看。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a gaze sweeping across a whole scene; the senses split into seeing everything from above, missing one thing in the sweep, forgiving by choice, and the old duty of watching over work.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一道扫过整片景物的目光；义项分成从高处看见全部、扫视中漏掉一处、存心放过过失，以及旧时看管工作的职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a west-facing window in a hillside inn, roofs and narrow alleys lying below it.
core.cn: 核心意象：山腰旅店朝西的窗，窗下摊着屋瓦与窄巷。
