branches.cn: 手指顺名单下滑、跳过一行

branches.en: a window above a harbour full of roofs
branches.cn: 港口上方看得见满片屋瓦的窗

branches.en: a manager quietly closing the file
branches.cn: 经理悄悄合上卷宗

branches.en: an old woman watching a row of sewing girls
branches.cn: 老妇人看着一排做针线的姑娘

branches.en: one skipped line, once an error and once a kindness
branches.cn: 同一行被跳过的地方，一次是错，一次是情

intro.en: The word sets the Old English prefix for over before the verb to look, and the same pieces recur in oversee, oversight and the inflected forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「在上」的前缀放在动词「看」前面，同样的部件还出现在 oversee、oversight 与各屈折形式里。

latinIntro.en: This compound is native Germanic and has no Latin family of its own; Latin super is a distant relative of the prefix, not a member of this word's history.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词是日耳曼语固有词，本身没有拉丁词族；拉丁语 super 只是前缀的远亲，不属于这个词的来历。

definition_zh: 整夜；一夜之间；过夜的；留宿
definition_en: through the whole night, happening with striking speed, arranged for or lasting one night, or to spend the night in a place
core_image: 凌晨的候车室里长椅上搭着外套，窗外雪还在下
scene: 凌晨的候车室里只剩下几个人，长椅上搭着外套，窗外的雪一直没停。The letters were flown overnight to the northern office.
sceneCN: 这里 overnight 是「整夜、在夜间」（第 1 个义项：副词，指整个夜里）；句意为信件连夜空运到北方的办事处，画面是凌晨候车室的长椅与不停的雪。

derivatives.zh: 由 overnight 加表示人或行程的后缀 -er 构成，义为「过夜的人；短途过夜行程」
由 overnight 与 bag 复合而成，义为「短途过夜用的小旅行包」

senses.title: Through the whole night
senses.definition: for or during the whole of the night, from evening until morning
senses.definitionCN: 从傍晚到早晨的整段时间里，或贯穿整个夜里
senses.example: We stayed overnight in a small hotel near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近一家小旅馆过了夜。
senses.why: The word is over plus night, so its first job is to stretch an action across the dark hours; nothing is quick yet, only continuous.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 over 加 night，最初的作用就是把一个动作拉长、横跨整个黑夜；此时还没有「快」的意思，只有「持续」。

senses.title: With striking speed
senses.definition: used of a change that seems to happen in a single night, so fast that people are caught unprepared
senses.definitionCN: 形容变化快得像只过了一夜，让人来不及准备
senses.example: The book became an overnight success.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书一夜之间成了畅销书。
senses.why: One night is a very short unit for a large change, so naming the night measures the surprise rather than the duration; the shorter the stretch, the more startling the result.
senses.whyCN: 对一场大变化来说，一夜是很短的计量单位，所以说「过了一夜」量的是惊讶程度而不是时长；时间越短，结果越惊人。

senses.title: Arranged for or lasting one night
senses.definition: describing a bag, stay, train or trip that belongs to a single night away from home
senses.definitionCN: 形容行李、逗留、列车或行程属于离家的一个晚上
senses.example: He packed an overnight bag and left before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他收拾了一个过夜的小包，天没亮就走了。
senses.why: Once the adverb marks a night, the same word can stand before a noun and label whatever belongs to that one night, so position becomes a kind of purpose.
senses.whyCN: 副词标出「一夜」之后，同一个词也能站到名词前面，标注属于那一夜的东西；位置义由此转成用途义。

senses.title: To spend the night somewhere
senses.definition: to stay in a place for the night, especially when travelling
senses.definitionCN: 在某处停留一夜，尤指旅行途中
senses.example: He overnighted in the city before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会前他在城里住了一夜。
senses.why: English turns many time words into verbs when travel needs a short label, and overnight simply means to do the thing the adverb describes: pass the night there.
senses.whyCN: 旅途中需要一个短说法时，英语常把时间词变成动词；overnight 作动词就是照副词所说的去做——在那里过完这一夜。

intro.en: Overnight joins two inherited Germanic words, first as a phrase for a stretch of time and later as an adjective and a verb of travel.
intro.cn: overnight 把两个日耳曼语固有词连在一起，先是表示一段时间跨度的短语，后来成为形容词与旅行动词。

items.en: Over and night both descend from reconstructed Germanic forms, and their union names time rather than place.
items.cn: over 与 night 都上溯到重构的日耳曼语形式，两者结合命名的是时间而不是地点。

items.en: Old English used ofer niht as a phrase for something lasting or happening through the dark hours.
items.cn: 古英语用 ofer niht 这个短语表示贯穿黑夜、或整夜发生的事。

items.en: Middle English wrote the two parts together and used the word for work and travel done between dusk and dawn.
items.cn: 中古英语把两部分合写，用这个词指黄昏到黎明之间完成的工作与行程。

items.en: Steam trains and mail coaches made the attributive use common in overnight bag, overnight train and overnight stay.
items.cn: 蒸汽列车与邮车让定语用法流行起来，出现 overnight bag、overnight train 与 overnight stay 这类说法。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative overnight success and a verb meaning to spend the night.
items.cn: 现代英语补上比喻性的 overnight success，以及表示「过夜」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived noun, the inflected forms and a compound; the near-meaning group gathers words of nightly time and of sudden change.
note.cn: 形近组收派生名词、各屈折形式与一个复合词；近义组收表示夜间时间与突然变化的词。

entries.definition: A person who stays overnight, or a short trip that lasts one night.
entries.definitionCN: 过夜的人，或只持续一晚的短途行程。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb, meaning stayed for the night.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，意为过了一夜。

entries.definition: The present participle of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的现在分词。

entries.definition: A small bag holding what one needs for one night away.
entries.definitionCN: 装一晚外出所需物品的小包。

entries.definition: Happening every night, or during each night.
entries.definitionCN: 每夜发生的，或在每夜期间发生的。

entries.definition: Quickly and without warning.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速且没有预兆地。

entries.definition: Happening immediately, with no delay at all.
entries.definitionCN: 立即发生、毫无延迟的。

entries.definition: Active at night rather than during the day.
entries.definitionCN: 在夜间而非白天活动的。

normalIntro.en: The word is over plus night, and its hooks return to the hours crossed, the surprise of a one-night change, and the bag packed for that night.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 over 加 night，记忆钩子都回到跨过去的那几个小时、一夜之变带来的惊讶，以及为那一夜收拾的包。

normal.en: Overnight is over plus night, so the word crosses a stretch of time rather than a distance.
normal.cn: overnight 是 over 加 night，跨过的是一段时间，而不是一段距离。

normal.en: The earliest use is a phrase, which is why the word still describes duration before it describes speed.
normal.cn: 最早的用法是短语，所以这个词先描述时长，后来才描述速度。

normal.en: The adjective follows the same picture and stands before whatever belongs to that one night, such as a bag or a train.
normal.cn: 形容词沿用同一画面，站在属于那一夜的东西前面，如包或列车。

normal.en: Overnight success measures surprise, not hours, so a fast rise needs only the name of one night.
normal.cn: overnight success 量的是惊讶而不是小时，所以飞快的崛起只需「一夜」这个名字。

normal.en: The verb simply asks someone to do what the adverb says, which is to pass the night in a place.
normal.cn: 动词只是让人照副词所说的去做，就是在某处过完这一夜。

abstract.en: A lit platform at dawn with coats over the benches is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 黎明时亮着灯的站台、长椅上搭着外套，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A single night between two ordinary days shows how a long change can be squeezed into one dark stretch.
abstract.cn: 两个平常日子之间的一夜，显示一场长变化如何被压进一段黑夜。

abstract.en: A small bag by the door is the word turned into an object ready to go.
abstract.cn: 门边一只小包，是这个词变成随时可以带走的物件。

examples.en: We stayed overnight in a small hotel near the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站附近一家小旅馆过了夜。

examples.en: The book became an overnight success.
examples.cn: 这本书一夜之间成了畅销书。

examples.en: He overnighted in the city before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前他在城里住了一夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃奈特」——欧沃熬了一整夜，天亮时事情已经变了模样。

root: overnight 由古英语 ofer（越过）与 niht（夜）合成，字面为「越过一夜」；两半都属日耳曼语固有词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stretch of time crossed in the dark; the senses move from lasting the whole night, to a change that seems that quick, to whatever belongs to one night, and to the act of staying.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是黑夜里被跨过去的一段时间；义项从持续整夜，转到快得像只过一夜的变化，转到属于那一夜的东西，最后转到过夜这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nearly empty waiting room before dawn, coats over the benches, snow still falling outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：天亮前几乎空了的候车室，外套搭在长椅上，窗外雪还没停。

branches.cn: 在黑夜中一路行驶的列车

branches.cn: 早饭时就已出名的书

branches.en: a small bag packed for one night

branches.cn: 同一夜，一次短得难以置信，一次只是被度过

intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「越过」的词放在「夜」前面，随后长出一个名词、一个复合词与一整套动词形式。

latinIntro.en: This is a native Germanic compound with no Latin family; Latin nox is only a distant Indo-European relative of night, not part of this word's descent.

definition_zh: 海外的；国外的；在海外；向海外；（总称）海外地区
definition_en: located, happening, or living across the sea in a foreign country; also the foreign countries taken together as a region
core_image: 站在海岸线上，越过一条水带望向另一块陆地
scene: 港口堆场里，贴着外文标签的集装箱被吊上货轮。The shipping clerk wrote overseas on the destination line, and the crane lifted the last box toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 overseas 是「海外的、国外的」（第 1 个义项：位于国外）；句意：报关员在目的地一栏写下“海外”，吊机把最后一个箱子吊向大海。图中可辨识物件：集装箱、外文标签、吊机、货轮、报关单、海平线；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 海外的（较早的变体拼法）
总部或驻地在海外的
在海外受训的
驶往海外的；发往国外的
在海外出生的

senses.title: Across the sea: located abroad
senses.definition: located or based in a country across the sea from the speaker's own
senses.definitionCN: 位于说话者本国之外、隔海相望的国家
senses.example: The company has three overseas branches.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有三家海外分公司。
senses.why: Over- means across or beyond, and sea is the water between the two shores. The reference point is always the speaker's own coast; what matters lies on the far side of the water.
senses.whyCN: over- 是“越过、在那边”，sea 是两岸之间的水。参照点始终是说话者自己这一侧的海岸，重要的事物在水的那一边。

senses.title: Coming from abroad
senses.definition: coming from or belonging to a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 来自外国或属于外国的
senses.example: Overseas visitors filled the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 海外游客挤满了博物馆。
senses.why: Here the direction reverses: the word marks not where the thing sits but where it came from. The sea is still the divider, only now the traffic crosses toward the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里方向反了过来：词标记的不是事物所在之处，而是它来自何处。海仍是分界，只是人流物流朝说话者这一侧越过来。

senses.title: Abroad: the adverbial direction
senses.definition: to or in a country across the sea
senses.definitionCN: 到海外，或在海外
senses.example: She moved overseas after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后她移居海外。
senses.why: English lets the same compound serve as an adverb without adding -ly. The phrase names a path, and the path crosses water, so no separate adverb form was ever needed.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个复合词直接作副词，不必加 -ly。这个短语命名的是一条路径，而路径要越过水，因此从来不需要另造副词形式。

senses.title: The overseas as a named region
senses.definition: the countries beyond the sea, taken together as a region or sphere of activity
senses.definitionCN: 隔海之外的国家，作为一个地区或活动领域的总称
senses.example: Sales in the overseas grew faster than at home.
senses.exampleCN: 海外市场的销售增长快于国内。
senses.why: A locational phrase can be nominalized: the far side stops being a direction and becomes a territory with a name. Business and journalism then speak of the overseas as a single place with its own figures.
senses.whyCN: 方位短语可以名词化：那边不再是方向，而变成一块有名字的地盘。商业与新闻于是把“海外”当作一个有自己的数字的单一地方来谈。

senses.title: Foreign affairs: the official sphere
senses.definition: relating to a country's interests and activities beyond its borders
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一国国境之外的利益与活动
senses.example: The ministry handles overseas affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 该部负责海外事务。
senses.why: Bureaucracy names the foreign sphere as an adjective, and activities there become a department's remit. The word turns geography into an administrative portfolio.
senses.whyCN: 官僚体系用形容词命名对外领域，那边的活动就变成一个部门的职责。这个词把地理变成了一份行政分工。

senses.title: Living abroad: of people
senses.definition: of a person or community, living in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指个人或群体侨居外国
senses.example: Overseas Chinese communities kept the festival alive.
senses.exampleCN: 海外华人社群把这个节日保留了下来。
senses.why: For people the compound marks residence rather than origin: the person's daily life has moved to the far shore, even if the passport and the language have not.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，这个词标记的是“居住地”而不是“来源地”：此人的日常生活已经移到海那边，即使护照与语言没有跟着变。

senses.title: Military deployment beyond the sea
senses.definition: of troops or bases, stationed in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指部队或基地驻扎在外国
senses.example: The unit served on overseas deployment for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队在海外部署了一年。
senses.why: Armies inherit the maritime image even when they fly. Overseas still means outside the home territory, and the word keeps military language politely vague about which country is meant.
senses.whyCN: 军队即使坐飞机也继承了这个航海意象。overseas 仍指本国领土之外，同时让军事语言礼貌地含糊，不必点明是哪一个国家。

senses.title: Historical euphemism: the colonies
senses.definition: in British usage, a polite word for the colonies and dominions, especially in the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 英国用法中，对殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤见于 20 世纪早期
senses.example: Wartime posters promised work in the overseas dominions.
senses.exampleCN: 战时海报承诺在海外自治领有工作机会。
senses.why: Overseas let speakers avoid the word colony. Distance across water replaced a political relationship that many preferred not to name, which is how a neutral geographic term became an instrument of imperial tact.
senses.whyCN: overseas 让说话者避开“colony”这个词。隔海的距离替代了一段许多人不想点明的政治关系，于是一个中性的地理词变成了帝国辞令里的委婉工具。

intro.en: Overseas is a native English compound of over and sea. The word is transparent, but the deeper origin of sea itself is not certain.
intro.cn: overseas 是 over 与 sea 构成的英语本族复合词。词形透明，但 sea 本身的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: The older form oversea is recorded as an adjective and adverb meaning 'across the sea, on the other side of the sea'.
items.cn: 较早的形式 oversea 记录于 15 世纪，作形容词与副词，意为“隔海、在海的那一边”。

items.en: Overseas appears with the same meaning and eventually displaces oversea in most contexts. Both are simply over + sea.
items.cn: overseas 于 16 世纪 80 年代出现，意义相同，最终在多数语境中取代 oversea。两者都只是 over + sea。

items.en: British imperial usage makes overseas a euphemism for the colonies and dominions, especially during the First World War.
items.cn: 英国帝国用语把 overseas 变成殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤在第一次世界大战期间。

items.en: The noun use is recorded: the overseas as the collective name for territories beyond the sea.
items.cn: 名词用法记录于 1919 年：the overseas 作为隔海之外领土的集合名称。

items.en: Trade, education, and the military keep the word busy: overseas market, overseas students, overseas deployment. The geographic frame stays neutral, which is exactly why it survives.
items.cn: 贸易、教育与军事让这个词持续活跃：海外市场、留学生、海外部署。它的地理框架保持中性，这也正是它存活下来的原因。

note.en: The first group collects over- words that look similar but do not mean across the sea. The second compares words for foreignness and distance.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 over-、外形相近却不表示“隔海”的词。第二组比较表示“异国、远方”的词。

entries.definition: to watch over and supervise work or people. It sounds almost the same but has no sea in it.
entries.definitionCN: 监督、管理工作的进行。读音几乎相同，但里面没有 sea。

entries.definition: larger than the standard size. It shares over- and the -size ending but means excess, not distance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过标准尺寸的。它同样带 over- 和 -size 结尾，但表示“过大”，而不是距离。

entries.definition: to express something more strongly than is justified. Its over- means too much, not across.
entries.definitionCN: 把话说得过头；夸大。它的 over- 表示“过分”，不是“越过”。

entries.definition: a loose garment worn over other clothes. It is over + all, and the plural -s can be mistaken for the -s of overseas.
entries.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的宽松工装。它是 over + all，复数 -s 容易被误当成 overseas 的 -s。

entries.definition: in or to a foreign country. It is only an adverb, while overseas can also be an adjective and a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在外国、到外国。它只能作副词，而 overseas 还能作形容词和名词。

entries.definition: belonging to a country other than one's own. It is the plain adjective and needs no sea, while overseas keeps the maritime image.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本国以外国家的。它是最朴素的形容词，不需要海；overseas 则保留了航海意象。

entries.definition: involving two or more nations. It stresses relations between states, while overseas stresses distance from home.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及两个或多个国家的。它强调国家之间的关系，overseas 强调与本土的距离。

entries.definition: away from the shore, especially of islands used for financial reasons. It is about distance from land, not about another country.
entries.definitionCN: 离岸的，尤指用于金融目的的海岛。它说的是离开陆地，而不是到另一个国家。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the over + sea picture, then three abstract images about distance and how it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 over + sea 画面的挂钩，再用三个关于距离及其用法的抽象画面。

normal.en: Say it as over-seas: over the seas, not over the sees. The plural seas are the water you cross.
normal.cn: 把它读成 over-seas：越过一片片海，而不是 over the sees。复数 seas 就是你越过的水。

normal.en: Look at a map: your finger starts on the home coast, crosses blue, and lands on another country. That finger path is overseas.
normal.cn: 看地图：手指从本国海岸出发，越过蓝色，落到另一个国家。那条手指路径就是 overseas。

normal.en: overseas students are students who crossed the sea to study; the sea is in the name, not in their luggage.
normal.cn: overseas students 是越过海来读书的学生；海在名字里，不在他们的行李里。

normal.en: The word has no -ly adverb form because it already works as an adverb: go overseas, live overseas.
normal.cn: 这个词没有 -ly 副词形式，因为它本身就能作副词：go overseas、live overseas。

normal.en: Overseas trade is trade that leaves the harbour; if the goods never touch water, the word still keeps the old picture.
normal.cn: overseas trade 是离开港口的贸易；即使货物从不碰水，这个词仍保留着旧画面。

abstract.en: Overseas is distance turned into a category: the far shore becomes an administrative box.
abstract.cn: overseas 是把距离变成一个分类：远岸被装进一个行政抽屉。

abstract.en: Every overseas is someone's home. The word marks the speaker's shore, not an absolute edge of the world.
abstract.cn: 每一个“海外”都是某些人的家。这个词标记的是说话者的海岸，而不是世界的绝对边缘。

abstract.en: The word is neutral geography doing political work: it can name a colony without saying colony.
abstract.cn: 这个词让中性的地理替政治干活：它可以指殖民地，却不必说出 colony。

examples.en: The firm opened an overseas office in Osaka last spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年春天在大阪开设了海外办事处。

examples.en: Many overseas students work part-time while they improve their English.
examples.cn: 许多留学生在提高英语的同时做兼职。

examples.en: The letters went overseas by ship and took six weeks to arrive.
examples.cn: 这些信件经海路寄往海外，走了六周才到。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 over 记成“越过”，sea 记成“海”：越过海的那一边，就是海外。
dict_mnemonic.text: over（越过）+ sea（海）+ -s → 海外的、在海外；海外地区

root: over（越过）+ sea（海）；sea 是日耳曼语固有词，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow the direction of travel: first something sits on the far shore, then it comes toward the speaker, then the word becomes a path, a named region, an official portfolio, a way of living, a military station, and finally a polite imperial word for the colonies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项顺着旅行的方向展开：先有东西位于远岸，再有东西朝说话者这边来，随后这个词变成一条路径、一块被命名的地区、一份官方职责、一种居住方式、一处军事驻地，最后成为帝国辞令里对殖民地的委婉说法。

core.en: A coastline, a band of water, and another land on the far side
core.cn: 一条海岸线、一条水带，以及水那边另一块陆地

branches.en: A place across the sea: the word locates something abroad.
branches.cn: 海那边的地方：这个词指某物位于国外。

branches.en: From a path to a place: the adverb of movement becomes a named region.
branches.cn: 从路径到地方：表示移动的副词变成一块被命名的地区。

branches.en: The official sphere: foreign affairs at a desk, and troops in the field.
branches.cn: 官方领域：办公桌上的对外事务，以及战场上的海外驻军。

branches.en: People: those who live and work across the sea.
branches.cn: 人：在海外生活与工作的那些人。

branches.en: Origin and old tongue: goods that come from across the sea, and the older British label for the colonies.
branches.cn: 来源与旧称：从海那边来的货物，以及英国旧时对殖民地的说法。

intro.en: Overseas is built from the over- prefix and the sea family. The items below include both true relatives and the nearest sea compounds, so the boundary of the family is visible.
intro.cn: overseas 由 over- 前缀和 sea 词族构成。下面既有真正的同族词，也有最接近的海事复合词，以便看清词族的边界。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer (PIE *uper), and sea is Old English sæ, from Proto-Germanic *saiwiz, whose deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer（原始印欧语 *uper），sea 是古英语 sæ，来自原始日耳曼语 *saiwiz，其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: across the sea; in or from a foreign country
items.meaningCN: 隔海；在海外或来自海外

items.meaning: the earlier adjective and adverb, now mostly replaced
items.meaningCN: 较早的形容词与副词形式，现已多被取代
items.example: An oversea cable was laid in 1866.
items.exampleCN: 一条海底电缆于 1866 年铺设。

items.meaning: the salt water that covers most of the earth
items.meaningCN: 覆盖地球大部分区域的咸水
items.example: The sea was calm that morning.
The seaward window caught the wind.

items.meaning: working or traveling on the sea
items.example: A seafaring family kept the old charts.
items.exampleCN: 一个航海世家保存着旧海图。

items.meaning: away from the shore; of financial islands
items.meaningCN: 离岸的；金融意义上的离岸

items.example: A transoceanic flight takes twelve hours.
items.exampleCN: 跨洋飞行需要十二小时。

definition_zh: 追上；超过；突然降临；压倒
definition_en: to catch up with and pass something moving ahead, to become greater than a rival or a figure, and to come upon someone suddenly
core_image: 后视镜里的车影越变越大，最后从侧旁滑到前方
scene: 雨夜的高速路上，一辆货车从后视镜里越来越大。On the wet highway, the truck pulled out and overtook the slow bus.
sceneCN: 这里 overtake 是「追上并超过」（第 1 个义项：同向赶超前方车辆）；句意为在湿滑的高速公路上，货车变道超过了那辆慢吞吞的巴士。图中可辨识物件：雨夜车灯、后视镜、慢行的巴士。

collocations.zh: 被突发事件赶超；形势令人措手不及

derivatives.zh: 由 overtake 加 -ing 构成，指超过前方车辆的动作，也可放在名词前作定语
overtake 的不规则过去式，表示已经完成的一次赶超

senses.title: To catch up with and pass a moving thing
senses.titleCN: 追上并超过（前方移动的人或车）
senses.definition: to reach the same point as a person or vehicle ahead and then move past it
senses.definitionCN: 赶上前方行进的人或车辆，到达同一点后再越过它
senses.example: The red bus overtook three lorries on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆红色巴士在山路上超过了三辆卡车。
senses.why: The word joins over, meaning across or beyond, with take, so its first sense is literally taking yourself across the path of what was ahead.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「越过、在上方」的 over 与 take 组合，字面就是把自己带过前方那辆车所在的位置，所以第一义是同向赶超。

senses.title: To become greater or more successful than
senses.definition: to become larger in amount, or more successful, than someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上变得更大，或在成就上变得更强，超过别人或旧有水平
senses.example: Online sales have overtaken those in the high street.
senses.exampleCN: 线上销售额已经超过了商业街实体店的销售额。
senses.why: Once over marks a line being crossed, the same picture fits a chart: one curve climbs past another, and the word needs no new machinery.
senses.whyCN: over 一旦表示跨过某条线，同一幅画面就能搬到图表上：一条曲线爬升到另一条之上，词义从空间顺理成章地扩到数量与地位。

senses.title: To come upon someone suddenly
senses.definition: of a storm, night, illness or event, to reach someone suddenly and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 指风暴、黑夜、疾病或事件毫无预兆地来到某人身上
senses.example: Night overtook the climbers before they reached the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者还没登上山脊，夜色就突然笼罩了他们。
senses.why: Something faster than you can overtake you from behind; the word keeps that racing image when darkness or misfortune arrives sooner than expected.
senses.whyCN: 比人走得更快的东西会从后面赶上人；当黑暗或灾祸比预想更早到来时，这个词保留了那种被追上、被盖过的赛跑画面。

senses.title: To overwhelm someone's control
senses.definition: of a feeling or bodily state, to become so strong that a person can no longer resist it
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或身体状态强烈到让人无法再抵抗
senses.example: He was overtaken by sleep halfway through the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影看到一半，他就被睡意压倒了。
senses.why: If an event can overtake a traveller, a wave of feeling can do the same inside a person: it catches up, passes the will, and takes over.
senses.whyCN: 既然事件能从外面赶上旅人，一股情绪也能在人心里做同样的事：它追上来，越过意志，接管了身体。

intro.en: Overtake is an English compound of over and take, recorded in the sense of catching up with someone in the sixteenth century; both parts are native Old English words, not Latin borrowings.
intro.cn: overtake 是 over 与 take 的英语复合词，十六世纪已有「赶上某人」的用法；两个部件都来自古英语本土词，不是拉丁语借词。

items.en: The ancestors are the Old English words ofer, meaning over or across, and tacan, meaning to seize or grasp.
items.cn: 源头是古英语 ofer（在上、越过）与 tacan（抓住、拿取）。

items.en: The two words were already used together in ordinary speech, but the modern spelling of the compound had not yet settled.
items.cn: 两个词在中古英语口语里已经常连用，只是现代拼写尚未定型。

items.en: Writers record overtake first for catching up with a rider or a runner on the road, a purely physical race.
items.cn: 十六世纪的文字里，overtake 先指在路上赶上骑手或奔跑者，是纯粹的身体竞速。

items.en: As trade and transport grew, the word was applied to ships, figures and rivals, so passing became surpassing.
items.cn: 随着贸易与运输发展，词义被用到船只、数字和对手身上，「越过」也就成了「超越」。

items.en: Modern English keeps the irregular overtook and overtaken, and adds the weather sense of being overtaken by night or a storm.
items.cn: 现代英语保留不规则变形 overtook 与 overtaken，并增加了被夜色或风暴突然笼罩的天气义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other take compounds; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for passing and beating in a race or a ranking.
note.cn: 形近组收其他含 take 的复合词；近义组收在赛道或排名上超过、胜过的动词。

entries.definition: A noun for the act of taking control of a company; the parts are the same but the order is reversed.
entries.definitionCN: 接管、收购一家公司的名词；部件与 overtake 相同，顺序相反。

entries.definition: To agree to do a task and begin it; it shares the take element.
entries.definitionCN: 同意承担并开始做某项任务；与 overtake 共享 take 这一部件。

entries.definition: To get hold of something or move it to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 拿到某物，或把它移到别处。

entries.definition: To go past a person or thing moving in the same direction.
entries.definitionCN: 同向经过某人或某物。

entries.definition: To become better or greater than someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 变得比某人或某物更好或更强。

entries.definition: To be greater than a number or limit.
entries.definitionCN: 大于某个数量或限度。

entries.definition: To reach the same level as someone who is ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 达到与前方某人相同的水平。

normalIntro.en: The word is a plain English compound, and every sense can be seen as one thing moving across the path of another.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是朴素的英语复合词，每个义项都可以看成一样东西越过另一样东西的路线。

normal.en: Over means across, take means to take yourself; overtake is to take yourself across the path of the car in front.
normal.cn: over 是越过，take 是把自己带到，overtake 就是把自己带到前面那辆车的路线上。

normal.en: The past forms are irregular: overtake becomes overtook, then overtaken, like take, took and taken.
normal.cn: 过去式不规则：overtake 变 overtook，再变 overtaken，和 take、took、taken 走同一条路。

normal.en: A takeover reverses the same two parts and names the act of seizing control of a company.
normal.cn: takeover 把这两个部件调换顺序，指夺取一家公司的控制权。

normal.en: In British traffic talk the overtaking lane is the one used to pass slower cars.
normal.cn: 英式交通说法里，overtaking lane 就是用来超过慢车的车道。

normal.en: Being overtaken by night is the same race image moved into the sky.
normal.cn: be overtaken by night 是把同一幅赛跑画面搬到了天上。

abstract.en: Speed turns space into advantage: what was behind you becomes what you leave behind.
abstract.cn: 速度把空间变成优势：原本在你身后的东西，变成被你留在身后的东西。

abstract.en: A curve crossing another curve on a chart is an overtaking with no wheels at all.
abstract.cn: 图表上一条曲线穿过另一条，是一次没有车轮的 overtake。

abstract.en: Anything that arrives faster than you expect has, in the language's eye, simply run past you.
abstract.cn: 任何比你预想更早到来的东西，在语言的眼里都只是从你身旁跑到了前面。

examples.en: The red bus overtook three lorries on the mountain road.
examples.cn: 那辆红色巴士在山路上超过了三辆卡车。

examples.en: Online sales have overtaken those in the high street.
examples.cn: 线上销售额已经超过了商业街实体店的销售额。

examples.en: Night overtook the climbers before they reached the ridge.
examples.cn: 登山者还没登上山脊，夜色就突然笼罩了他们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃太克」——听成「欧了，我还得再快一点」，超车时喊一声，记住 overtake 是超过。

root: 英语本土复合词：over（越过、在上）加 take（拿、带）；没有直接对应的拉丁同族词，同族词多为 take 的复合形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is passing something ahead; the senses then move from road traffic to rankings, to sudden nightfall, and finally to feelings that take control.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是越过前方之物；义项从道路上的超车，延伸到排名上的超越、夜色的突然降临，最后是接管身心的强烈感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car growing larger in the mirror, sliding past, and settling in front.
core.cn: 核心意象：后视镜里的车越来越大，从旁边滑过，最后稳稳落在前头。

branches.en: a car sliding past a slower bus in the rain
branches.cn: 雨中一辆车从慢巴士旁滑过

branches.en: a chart line climbing above the old record
branches.cn: 一条曲线爬过旧纪录

branches.en: a young runner beating a veteran champion
branches.cn: 年轻选手击败老冠军

branches.en: night falling on climbers still below the ridge
branches.cn: 夜色落在还没上山脊的登山者身上

branches.en: a passenger nodding off before the film ends
branches.cn: 乘客没等电影结束就睡着了

intro.en: The word is built from two Old English pieces and then carried by later compounds of take; the structure is English, not Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语部件构成，后来又被一系列含 take 的复合词延续；结构属于英语，不属于拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; both of its parts are native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的两个部件都来自古英语本土词。

items.meaning: the act of passing a vehicle

definition_zh: 欠（钱）；归功于；应给予；理应
definition_en: to have money still to pay, to be grateful to someone or something for a result, or to be under an obligation to give something
core_image: 账本上一行没有划掉的数字，提醒你还欠着别人
scene: 月底的餐桌上，一张写满数字的账单被推到对方面前。I still owe you two hundred yuan for the tickets.
sceneCN: 这里 owe 是「欠钱」（第 1 个义项：还欠着钱没付）；句意为我还欠你买票的两百块钱。图中可辨识物件：账单、餐盘、被推到桌对面的手势。

derivatives.zh: 由 owe 加 -ing 构成，表示「欠着的、尚未支付的」，常见于 owing to 表示「由于」
owe 的过去式与过去分词，表示已经欠下、曾被欠

senses.title: To have a debt to pay
senses.definition: to have borrowed money or goods and not yet paid for them
senses.definitionCN: 借了钱或拿了东西，还没有付清
senses.example: I still owe the shop twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 我还欠那家店二十英镑。
senses.why: The Old English verb āgan meant to possess; a debt is what another person still holds a claim on, so the word came to name the part not yet handed over.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 āgan 本义是拥有；债务正是别人仍握有权利的那部分，于是这个词转指你还没交还出去的东西。

senses.title: To be grateful for a result
senses.definition: to be grateful to a person or thing because they made a good result possible
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人或某物促成了好结果而感激他
senses.example: She owes her career to a teacher who believed in her.
senses.exampleCN: 她把事业归功于一位相信她的老师。
senses.why: If a person still holds what you received, the debt can be a debt of gratitude; the ledger moves from money to credit for a result.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人仍握着你得到的好处，这份债就成了感激之债；账本从金钱转成了对某份成果的功劳记录。

senses.title: To be under an obligation to give
senses.definition: to be obliged to give someone something such as an apology, an explanation or attention
senses.definitionCN: 有义务给某人某样东西，如道歉、解释或关注
senses.example: You owe him an explanation for leaving so suddenly.
senses.exampleCN: 你突然离开，欠他一个解释。
senses.why: A debt need not be money: any unfinished obligation, from an apology to a phone call, sits in the same place on the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 债不一定是钱：任何没完成的义务，从一句道歉到一个电话，都记在账本的同一栏。

senses.title: To be morally required to do something
senses.definition: in the phrase owe it to someone, to be morally required to do something for that person, especially for oneself
senses.definitionCN: 在 owe it to someone 这一说法里，指道义上应该为某人做某事，尤其应为自己的利益去做
senses.example: You owe it to yourself to take a real holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 你理应给自己放一个真正意义上的假。
senses.why: The same ledger can record a duty owed to oneself, which is why the phrase turns a moral claim into a kind of unpaid account.
senses.whyCN: 同一本账也能记下一个人对自己的责任，所以这个说法把道义要求写成了一笔尚未付清的账。

intro.en: Owe goes back to Old English āgan, to have or to possess; its modern meaning of debt grew out of the idea of something still held by another party.
intro.cn: owe 源自表示「拥有、持有」的古英语 āgan；今天「欠」的意思，是从「东西仍被另一方握有」这一观念长出来的。

items.en: The verb āgan meant to own, to have and to hold; a person could āgan land, cattle or money.
items.cn: 动词 āgan 意为拥有、持有；人可以拥有土地、牲畜或钱财。

items.en: A past form āhte began to take the sense of having a claim upon someone, and this is the seed of the debt sense.
items.cn: 过去式 āhte 开始带有「对某人拥有权利」的意思，这就是债务义的种子。

items.en: Middle English owen already meant both to possess and to be obliged to pay, depending on the sentence.
items.cn: 中古英语的 owen 已同时表示「拥有」与「有义务支付」，要看句子而定。

items.en: As own took over the plain sense of possession, owe was left with debt and obligation, and the split became permanent.
items.cn: 随着 own 接掌了纯粹的「拥有」义，owe 只剩下债务与义务，这一分工最终固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps owed and owing, and the phrase owing to, where a debt becomes the reason for something.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 owed 与 owing，以及 owing to，在那里一笔债变成了某事的原因。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the old verb of holding and its surviving relatives; the near-meaning group follows debt, gratitude and its opposite, repayment.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「持有」的旧动词及仍在使用的亲属词展开；近义组沿着债务、感激以及它的另一面——偿还——展开。

entries.definition: To possess something as property; the two words split from the same Old English verb.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物；这两个词由同一个古英语动词分出。

entries.definition: The old past tense of owe, now a modal verb for duty.
entries.definitionCN: owe 历史上的过去式，今为表示义务的情态动词。

entries.definition: Still unpaid, or, in owing to, because of.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未支付的；在 owing to 中表示「由于」。

entries.definition: Owing money, or grateful for help received.
entries.definitionCN: 负债的；受恩的。

entries.definition: To say that something is caused by a particular person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事归因于某人或某物。

entries.definition: To give someone praise for an achievement.
entries.definitionCN: 把成就归功于某人。

entries.definition: To pay back money that was borrowed.
entries.definitionCN: 偿还借来的钱。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old verb of holding whose debt sense survived while own took the plain sense of possession.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本是表示「持有」的旧动词，债务义留了下来，而纯粹的「拥有」义交给了 own。

normal.en: The Old English verb meant to have; a debt is what another person still has over you.
normal.cn: 古英语动词本义是持有；债务就是别人仍对你持有的一份东西。

normal.en: Own and owe split from the same verb: own keeps the possession, owe keeps the obligation.
normal.cn: own 与 owe 由同一个动词分出：own 留下拥有，owe 留下义务。

normal.en: Owing to works like a note on a receipt: one thing is charged to the account of another.
normal.cn: owing to 像收据上的备注：一件事被记到另一件事的账上。

normal.en: Ought is the old past tense of owe, which is why both still deal with duty.
normal.cn: ought 是 owe 旧的过去式，所以两者至今都在谈「应当」。

normal.en: You can owe an apology as easily as money; both are entries not yet settled.
normal.cn: 道歉和钱一样可以欠；两者都是还没结清的一笔。

abstract.en: A debt is a thread that keeps two people connected until it is paid.
abstract.cn: 债是一根线，在付清之前把两个人连着。

abstract.en: Gratitude is a ledger with no money in it, only names.
abstract.cn: 感激是一本没有钱数、只有名字的账。

abstract.en: To owe is to admit that part of what you are came from somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 欠，就是承认你之所以成为现在的样子，有一部分来自别处。

examples.en: I still owe the shop twenty pounds.
examples.cn: 我还欠那家店二十英镑。

examples.en: She owes her career to a teacher who believed in her.
examples.cn: 她把事业归功于一位相信她的老师。

examples.en: You owe him an explanation for leaving so suddenly.
examples.cn: 你突然离开，欠他一个解释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧」——欠债的人看到账单只会喊一声「欧」，记住 owe 是欠。

root: 古英语 āgan（拥有、持有）到中古英语 owen；拥有义后来交给 own，owe 专指欠与归功于。同族词还有 ought、owing。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unsettled claim; the senses spread from money to gratitude, to social obligations, and finally to duties owed to oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一笔没结清的权利；义项从金钱扩展到感激、社交义务，最后落到对自己也欠着一份责任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line in a notebook that has not been crossed out.
core.cn: 核心意象：本子上那一行始终没有划掉的记录。

branches.en: a shopkeeper's notebook with an unpaid line
branches.cn: 店主本子上没划掉的一行

branches.en: a teacher named in a speech of thanks
branches.cn: 致谢演讲里被点名的老师

branches.en: an unsent apology waiting on a phone screen
branches.cn: 手机屏幕上一条没发出的道歉

branches.en: a tired worker finally booking a holiday
branches.cn: 疲惫的职员终于订下了假期

branches.en: a debt to another person and a debt to oneself
branches.cn: 欠别人的一笔，欠自己的一笔

intro.en: The forms come from one Old English verb of holding, with an old past tense that survives as a modal verb and an -ing form that still marks an unpaid sum.
intro.cn: 这些形式都出自同一个表示「持有」的古英语动词，其中一个旧过去式作为情态动词留存，一个 -ing 形式仍表示未付的款项。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it descends from an Old English verb of holding.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它出自一个表示「持有」的古英语动词。

items.meaningCN: 应当，源自 owe 的旧过去式

definition_zh: 自己的；本人的；自己的东西；拥有；承认
definition_en: belonging to oneself, the thing that belongs to oneself, and to have something as property or to admit a fact
core_image: 钥匙串上那把只配你家门的钥匙
scene: 搬家那天，每只纸箱上都写着同一个名字。After the move she kept her own keys in a small tin box.
sceneCN: 这里 own 是「自己的」（第 1 个义项：属于本人的）；句意为搬完之后，她把自己的钥匙收在一只小铁盒里。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、钥匙、铁盒。

pos.zh: 自己的东西（用在物主词之后）

derivatives.zh: 由 own 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，指拥有某物的人
由 owner 加 -ship 构成，指所有权、产权
home 与 owner 复合而成，指自有住房者

senses.title: Belonging to a particular person
senses.definition: belonging to a particular person rather than to anyone else
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个特定的人，而不是任何别人
senses.example: She keeps her own keys in a small tin box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己的钥匙放在一个小铁盒里。
senses.why: The adjective began as a past participle meaning possessed; it points back at the person who holds the thing, so it always answers the question whose.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最初是表示「被拥有」的过去分词；它回指持有东西的那个人，所以总在回答「谁的」这一问题。

senses.title: The thing that belongs to oneself
senses.definition: used after a possessive word to mean the particular thing or person that belongs to someone
senses.definitionCN: 用在物主词之后，指属于某人的那样东西或那个人
senses.example: He wanted a desk of his own, away from the shared one.
senses.exampleCN: 他想要一张属于自己的桌子，不再和人共用。
senses.why: When the noun is already clear from context, own can stand alone after words like my or his, carrying the idea of possession without naming the object again.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已由上下文点明，own 可以跟在 my、his 这类物主词后单独使用，重复「属于」这层意思而不再说出物品的名字。

senses.title: To have something as property
senses.definition: to legally or actually have something as property
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上或事实上把某物作为财产持有
senses.example: Her family owns a small orchard outside the town.
senses.exampleCN: 她家在城外拥有一片小果园。
senses.why: The verb comes from the same Old English word for having and holding; possession is the plain centre that the adjective later uses to point at a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自同一个表示「持有、拥有」的古英语词；持有正是这个词最朴素的中心，形容词后来只是用它回指持有的人。

senses.title: To admit a fact or fault
senses.definition: to admit that something is true, especially something you would rather not say
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，尤指本不愿说出口的事
senses.example: She owned that the plan had been too rushed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认那个计划太仓促了。
senses.why: To own a fact is to accept it as part of what is yours, which is why British English uses own up for confessing a fault.
senses.whyCN: 承认一个事实，就是把它当成属于自己的东西接受下来；英式英语里 own up 表示坦白，正由此而来。

intro.en: Own has two faces: an Old English past participle meaning possessed, which became the adjective, and an Old English verb meaning to have, which became the modern verb.
intro.cn: own 有两副面孔：一个是表示「被拥有」的古英语过去分词，后来成了形容词；另一个是表示「持有」的古英语动词，后来成了今天的动词。

items.en: The adjective āgen was a past participle of the verb āgan and meant possessed or belonging to someone.
items.cn: 形容词 āgen 是动词 āgan 的过去分词，意为「被拥有的、属于某人的」。

items.en: The verb āgan meant to have, to hold and to own land or goods, and it is also the source of owe.
items.cn: 动词 āgan 意为持有、握着，拥有土地或财物，它同时也是 owe 的来源。

items.en: Middle English owen served as both adjective and verb, and the spelling with w replaced the old g sound in writing.
items.cn: 中古英语的 owen 同时作形容词和动词，书写上用 w 代替了旧的 g 音。

items.en: Own up appears in the sense of admitting a fault, extending possession to the idea of accepting a fact as one's own.
items.cn: own up 在十六世纪出现「承认过失」的意思，把「拥有」扩展到「把事实认作自己的」。

items.en: Modern English keeps own as adjective, pronoun and verb, while the related verb owe carries the debt side of the old word.
items.cn: 现代英语让 own 同时作形容词、代词和动词，而由同一旧词分出的 owe 承担了债务那一面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the family built on this old verb of holding; the near-meaning group follows possession and, separately, the act of admitting.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个表示「持有」的旧动词所建的词族展开；近义组一面收「拥有」，一面收「承认」。

entries.definition: A person who owns something; own plus the person suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的人；own 加表示人的后缀 -er。

entries.definition: The state or legal right of owning something.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的状态或法定权利。

entries.definition: To be in debt; it split from the same Old English verb as own.
entries.definitionCN: 欠债；与 own 由同一个古英语动词分出。

entries.definition: To have something, especially as property.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，尤指作为财产。

entries.definition: To have something in your hands or under your control.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拿在手里，或置于自己控制之下。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true, often unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，常带不情愿的意味。

normalIntro.en: The word carries both a pointing adjective and a holding verb, and the family around it keeps turning possession into people and rights.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时带着一个指认的形容词和一个持有的动词，它周围的词族不断把「拥有」变成人和权利。

normal.en: Āgan in Old English meant to have; both own and owe grew from it, one as possession, the other as debt.
normal.cn: 古英语 āgan 意为持有；own 与 owe 都由它长出，一个拿拥有，一个拿欠债。

normal.en: The -er on owner marks the person, while own itself marks the thing or the act.
normal.cn: owner 上的 -er 标出人，而 own 本身标出的是东西或动作。

normal.en: Own up is possession turned inward: you take a fault and call it yours.
normal.cn: own up 是拥有向内转：你把一个过失拿过来，说它是自己的。

normal.en: On your own means you are the only person in the picture, with nobody else to lean on.
normal.cn: on your own 意味着画面里只有你一个人，没有别人可以依靠。

normal.en: A room of your own is a place the possessive word cannot share with anyone else.
normal.cn: a room of your own 是一处物主词不肯与任何人分享的地方。

abstract.en: Owning is a social fact disguised as a grammar word: it always needs someone to point at.
abstract.cn: 拥有是一个装扮成语法词的社会事实：它总要指向某个人。

abstract.en: The same word for having and for confessing hints that admitting is a way of taking responsibility as yours.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既表示拥有又表示承认，暗示坦白就是把责任认领为自己的。

abstract.en: An owner is a name attached to a thing, and the thing may outlast the name.
abstract.cn: 所有者是附在物品上的一个名字，而物品往往比名字活得更久。

examples.en: She keeps her own keys in a small tin box.
examples.cn: 她把自己的钥匙放在一个小铁盒里。

examples.en: Her family owns a small orchard outside the town.
examples.cn: 她家在城外拥有一片小果园。

examples.en: She owned that the plan had been too rushed.
examples.cn: 她承认那个计划太仓促了。

root: 古英语 āgan（持有）的过去分词 āgen 成为形容词「自己的」，同一动词又直接发展出动词「拥有」；「欠」义则由 owe 承担。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to a particular person; the adjective points at the owner, the pronoun leaves the noun unsaid, and the verb extends to holding property and to admitting a fault.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是属于某个特定之人的东西；形容词指向主人，代词省去名词，动词则扩展到持有财产与承认过失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key that fits one door and no other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把只配得上自家那扇门的钥匙。

branches.en: a name written inside a school coat
branches.cn: 校服内侧写着的名字

branches.en: a desk that nobody else may use
branches.cn: 不许别人用的那张书桌

branches.en: an orchard with a deed in a drawer
branches.cn: 抽屉里放着地契的果园

branches.en: a confession said out loud at last
branches.cn: 终于说出口的一句坦白

branches.en: a corner of a shared room marked by one chair
branches.cn: 公用房间里被一把椅子标出的角落

intro.en: Two Old English shapes meet in this word, a participle that became the adjective and a verb of holding; English suffixes then build the people and rights around it.
intro.cn: 这个词里汇合了两个古英语形态，一个成了形容词的分词，和一个表示持有的动词；英语后缀随后在它周围造出人与权利。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its two grammatical lives both come from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的两种语法身份都来自古英语。

definition_en: a person who owns something, especially the person with the legal title to property or the head of a business

sceneCN: 这里 owner 是「物主、所有者」（第 1 个义项：拥有某物的人）；句意为新店主把店面刷成了深绿色。图中可辨识物件：旧书店门脸、油漆桶、刷子。

由 owner 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，指无主的

senses.title: A person who owns something
senses.definition: a person who has something as property, whether a house, a car or a pet
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为财产持有的人，可以是房子、汽车或宠物
senses.example: The owner of the little dog waited by the gate every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那只小狗的主人每天傍晚都在门口等。
senses.why: Owner is own plus -er, the suffix that turns an action into a person, so the word names whoever holds the property.
senses.whyCN: owner 是 own 加 -er，这个后缀把动作变成人，所以这个词指持有那件财产的人。

senses.title: The person with the legal title
senses.definition: the person or company recorded in law as holding title to a property
senses.definitionCN: 在法律记录上持有某项财产所有权的人或公司
senses.example: The land owner refused to sell to the developer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位土地产权人拒绝把地卖给开发商。
senses.why: Because the verb own covers legal possession, adding -er produces the party a deed or register points to when ownership is disputed.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词 own 涵盖法律上的持有，加上 -er 就造出契据或登记簿在产权争议中指认的那一方。

senses.title: The head of a business
senses.definition: the person who runs and profits from a shop, company or sports club
senses.definitionCN: 经营一家店铺、公司或体育俱乐部并从中获利的人
senses.example: The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
senses.exampleCN: 新店主把店面的门脸重新刷成了深绿色。
senses.why: A business is treated as a thing that can be owned, so the same suffix names the person at the top of it, from a corner shop to a football club.
senses.whyCN: 生意被看作可以拥有的一样东西，于是同一个后缀也用来指站在它顶端的人，从街角小店到足球俱乐部都适用。

intro.en: Owner is an English formation from own and the suffix -er; no Latin ancestor is involved, and the word appears in Middle English.
intro.cn: owner 由 own 加后缀 -er 构成的英语词，不涉及拉丁语祖先，中古英语时期已经出现。

items.en: The base is āgan, to have and to hold, with its participle āgen meaning belonging to someone.
items.cn: 词基是 āgan，意为持有、拥有，其分词 āgen 意为「属于某人的」。

items.en: Middle English ownen, to possess, supplied the stem, and the agent suffix -er was added to name the person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ownen（拥有）提供了词干，再加上表示行为者的后缀 -er 用来指人。

items.en: Forms such as ownere appear in records of land and goods, where a named person had to answer for what was held.
items.cn: ownere 这类形式出现在土地与货物的记录里，那里需要一个具名的人为所持之物负责。

items.en: With industry and property law, owner spread to shops, ships and companies, and compounds such as landowner became common.
items.cn: 随着工业与财产法的发展，owner 扩展到店铺、船只和公司，landowner 之类的复合词也变得常见。

items.en: Modern English uses owner for people and ownership for the abstract right, keeping the two endings clearly apart.
items.cn: 现代英语用 owner 指人，用 ownership 指抽象的权利，两个后缀分工清楚。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the base word and the suffixes that rebuild it; the near-meaning group gathers other names for the person who holds property.
note.cn: 形近组沿基础词和重建它的后缀展开；近义组收其他指「持有财产之人」的说法。

entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，或指属于自己的。

entries.definition: The legal right or state of owning something.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的法定权利或状态。

entries.definition: The owner of a business or property.

entries.definition: A person who has something in their possession.
entries.definitionCN: 占有某物的人。

entries.definition: A person who owns a house or land and rents it out.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有房屋或土地并出租的人。

normalIntro.en: The word adds one suffix to a verb of holding, and everything else in the family simply adds another suffix to that person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只是给表示持有的动词加了一个后缀，词族里其余的词又在这个「人」上继续加后缀。

normal.en: Owner is own plus -er: the suffix does nothing but turn holding into a person.
normal.cn: owner 是 own 加 -er：这个后缀只做一件事，把持有变成人。

normal.en: Ownership adds -ship to owner and turns the person back into an abstract right.
normal.cn: ownership 在 owner 后加 -ship，又把人变回一种抽象权利。

normal.en: Landowner and homeowner simply put the kind of property in front of the person.
normal.cn: landowner 与 homeowner 只是把财产种类放在人前面。

normal.en: The owner of a shop and the owner of a dog share one word because both answer for something.
normal.cn: 店主和狗主人共用一个词，因为两者都要为某样东西负责。

normal.en: Owe, own and owner all come from the same Old English verb of holding.
normal.cn: owe、own 与 owner 都来自同一个表示持有的古英语动词。

abstract.en: A person's name on a deed is a way of making a claim visible to everyone else.
abstract.cn: 地契上写下一个人的名字，是把一份主张变得人人可见的方法。

abstract.en: Ownership can be sold, lent or fought over, while the owner may change many times.
abstract.cn: 所有权可以被出售、出借或争夺，而所有者可能换了许多次。

abstract.en: Every owner is also someone who answers for what happens to the thing owned.
abstract.cn: 每个所有者同时也是那个要为所拥有之物的遭遇负责的人。

examples.en: The owner of the little dog waited by the gate every evening.
examples.cn: 那只小狗的主人每天傍晚都在门口等。

examples.en: The land owner refused to sell to the developer.
examples.cn: 那位土地产权人拒绝把地卖给开发商。

examples.en: The new owner repainted the shop front in dark green.
examples.cn: 新店主把店面的门脸重新刷成了深绿色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧呢」——问这东西是谁的，回答一声「欧呢」，就是主人；记住 owner 是所有者。

root: own（拥有）加 -er（表示人）构成；own 来自古英语 āgan（持有），与 owe 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the person behind a piece of property; the senses narrow into the legal title holder and widen again to the head of a business.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是财产背后那个人；义项一面收窄到法定产权人，一面又扩展到企业的老板。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name on a doorplate, and the one key that turns in the lock below it.
core.cn: 核心意象：门牌上写着名字，门下的锁只认那一把钥匙。

branches.en: a dog waiting by a gate for its person
branches.cn: 一条狗在门口等它的主人

branches.en: a deed with one name written on it
branches.cn: 写着一个人名字的地契

branches.en: a shopkeeper unlocking the door at dawn
branches.cn: 店主在清晨开门

branches.en: a club owner watching from the stands
branches.cn: 俱乐部老板在看台上观战

branches.en: a key turning in a lock that belongs to one name
branches.cn: 钥匙转动，锁只属于一个名字

intro.en: The word is a verb of holding plus the English person suffix -er, and the rest of the family adds suffixes to that person.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示持有的动词加上英语中表示人的后缀 -er，词族其余部分再在这个「人」上继续加后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it is an English noun built on a native verb plus -er.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它是由本土动词加 -er 构成的英语名词。

items.meaningCN: 做某事或持有某物的人

definition_zh: 所有权；拥有；归属关系
definition_en: the state or legal right of possessing something, or the relation by which a thing belongs to a person
core_image: 一枚刻着名字的铜牌钉在门上，钥匙挂在旁边，名字在牌上的人就有权处置屋内之物
scene: 产权登记处把房屋过户到买方名下，登记簿上的名字一换，处置权随之转移。The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
sceneCN: 这里指「对某物享有法律上的所有权」，对应第 1 个义项：可以占有、使用与处置的权利；句意为登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。画面要点：门上的铜牌、挂着的钥匙、登记簿；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 所有权；拥有（不可数，常后接表示所属物的介词短语，指明所拥有之物）

derivatives.zh: 所有者；物主（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）
共有；共同所有（表示「共同」的前缀与所有权一词复合，指所有权由多人分享）
拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）

senses.title: The legal right to dispose of a thing
senses.titleCN: 对物进行处置的法律权利
senses.definition: the legal power to use, sell, give away or exclude others from a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用、出售、赠予某物并排除他人使用的法律权力
senses.example: The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
senses.exampleCN: 产权登记处把房屋过户给买方，登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。
senses.why: The word joins the verb 'to have' to a suffix for a condition, so it names a state of having that the law will protect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示「拥有」的动词与表状态的后缀结合，命名一种法律会保护的有有状态。

senses.title: Holding something in fact
senses.definition: the actual possession of a thing, whether or not the law recognises a title
senses.definitionCN: 实际持有某物，无论法律是否承认其权属
senses.example: Ownership of the keys does not always mean ownership of the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 拿着钥匙并不总意味着拥有这套公寓。
senses.why: Possession and title can come apart, and the word sometimes describes the plain fact of having rather than the right to have.
senses.whyCN: 占有与权属可以分开，这个词有时描述「手上确实有」这一事实，而不是「有权拥有」。

senses.title: The relation of belonging
senses.definition: the link by which a thing is attributed to a person, so that it answers to that person's name
senses.definitionCN: 某物被归到某人名下、对其名字作出回应的那种联系
senses.example: Ownership of the manuscript is disputed between two libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿的归属在两家图书馆之间存有争议。
senses.why: Beyond the right and the fact lies a relation: the thing belongs to someone, and that belonging is what the noun most abstractly names.
senses.whyCN: 在权利与事实之外还有一层关系：物属于某人，而这种归属正是这个名词最抽象地命名的东西。

senses.title: Shareholding and proprietorship
senses.definition: the holding of shares in a company, or the position of a person who owns a firm
senses.definitionCN: 持有公司股份，或拥有某企业的业主地位
senses.example: Foreign ownership of the airline was capped at a fixed share.
senses.exampleCN: 该航空公司的外资持股被限定在固定比例内。
senses.why: When firms replace land as the main object of wealth, the same noun measures who holds the shares.
senses.whyCN: 当企业取代土地成为财富的主要对象，同一个名词就用来衡量谁持有股份。

senses.title: Public versus private regimes
senses.titleCN: 公有与私有的制度之分
senses.definition: the system under which the means of production or a service is held by the state or by private persons
senses.definitionCN: 生产资料或某项服务由国家持有还是由私人持有的制度安排
senses.example: The dispute was about ownership of the water supply, not about its price.
senses.exampleCN: 争论在于供水归谁所有，而不在于水价。
senses.why: Ownership becomes a political question once whole industries rather than single objects are at stake.
senses.whyCN: 一旦涉及的是整个行业而不是单件物品，所有权就成了政治问题。

senses.title: Personal responsibility for a task
senses.definition: the attitude of treating a problem or project as one's own, with the duty to see it through
senses.definitionCN: 把某个问题或项目当作自己的事、并承担完成责任的态度
senses.example: The team asked each member to take ownership of one part of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 团队要求每位成员对计划的一部分负起责任。
senses.why: Modern management borrowed the legal word and stripped the title from it, leaving only the sense of treating the work as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 现代管理借用了这个法律词，抽去了权属，只留下「把工作当作自己的事」这一层。

senses.title: Attribution of a work to its author
senses.definition: the legal and moral link between a creative work and the person who made it
senses.definitionCN: 创造性作品与其创作者之间的法律与道义联系
senses.example: Ownership of the copyright passed to the publisher for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 著作权中的财产权在十年内转给了出版方。
senses.why: A text or a design can belong to someone too, so the noun extends from goods to works of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 文本或设计同样可以属于某人，因此这个名词从货物延伸到心智作品。

senses.title: Tenure of land in older law
senses.definition: the holding of land under a lord or a superior, with duties attached, rather than outright title
senses.definitionCN: 在领主或上级之下持有土地并附带义务，而不是绝对的所有权
senses.example: In that period ownership of land carried service as well as rent.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个时期，土地保有权既带来地租，也带来服役义务。
senses.why: Before absolute title was common, holding land meant holding it of someone, and the word recorded that layered relation.
senses.whyCN: 在绝对所有权普及之前，持有土地意味着从某人那里持有，这个词记录了那种分层的关系。

intro.en: Ownership joins the Old English verb agan 'to have, possess' to the suffix -ship, which came from a word for shape or condition. Both parts are Germanic, and the compound is a native English formation rather than a borrowing.
intro.cn: ownership 由古英语动词 agan「拥有、占有」加后缀 -ship 构成，而后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词。两部分都属日耳曼语，这个复合词是英语本族造词，而不是借词。

items.en: Agan 'to have, to possess' is the verb behind own, and it is Germanic, with recorded relatives in other old Germanic languages.
items.cn: agan 意为「有、占有」，是 own 背后的动词，属日耳曼语，在其他古老日耳曼语言中有可考的同族词。

items.en: The reconstructed verb is posited with a star; the deeper Indo-European root is also a reconstruction, so the earliest layer is not directly attested.
items.cn: 重构的动词形式以带星号的方式拟出；更深的印欧语词根同样属重构，因此最早的层次没有直接文献实证。

items.en: The suffix came from a word meaning 'shape, condition', and it built nouns for states, offices and skills.
items.cn: 这个后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词，用来构成表示状态、职位与技艺的名词。

items.en: The compound joined the two and named the condition of one who has something, at first in ordinary rather than legal language.
items.cn: 这个复合词把两者结合，命名「拥有某物者的状态」，最初用于日常语言而非法律语言。

items.en: Lawyers later separated ownership from mere holding, giving the noun a technical sense that possession alone does not fill.
items.cn: 法学家后来把所有权与单纯的占有分开，使这个名词获得一个单靠占有无法填补的专业含义。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word also came to mean personal responsibility for a task. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词也开始指对任务负起个人责任。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built from the same verb or looks close to it; the second group gives near alternatives from law, accounting and plain possession.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个动词构成或与它形近；第二组是来自法律、会计与日常占有三个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: To possess, or belonging to oneself, as in one's own; it is the source word, while the entry noun names the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有，或属于自己，如「自己的」；它是来源词，而本名词命名那种关系。

entries.definition: The person who holds title to a thing; the suffix marks a person, so the word cannot name the relation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物持有权属的人；后缀标示人，因此这个词不能命名关系本身。

entries.definition: Still to be paid, as in an owing sum; it comes from the verb owe, which is a different word from own.
entries.definitionCN: 尚待支付的，如「欠款」；它出自动词「欠」，与「拥有」是不同的词。

entries.definition: A person who owns the home he lives in; it joins the owner word to a word for occupying.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有并居住在自己房屋的人；它把「所有者」与「占用」两个词连在一起。

entries.definition: The fact of having something under one's control; it can exist without legal title, which is why the two are distinguished.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律权属而存在，因此两者被区分开。

entries.definition: The status of an owner, especially of a business; it is close in meaning but more formal and more often used of firms.
entries.definitionCN: 所有人的身份，尤指企业所有人；它意思相近，但更正式，也更常用于企业。

entries.definition: The legal right to own property, or the document proving it; it is the lawyer's word for the proof rather than the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有财产的合法权利，或证明它的文件；它是法学家用来指证明而非关系的词。

entries.definition: The care and control of a person or thing, often without ownership; a custodian may hold what belongs to another.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或在物的照管与控制，往往不含所有权；保管人可以持有属于他人之物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Old English verb for having, the native suffix for a condition, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古英语中表示「有」的动词、本族语中表状态的后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a name on a door: the thing answers to that name.
normal.cn: 核心是门上刻着的一个名字：那件东西对那个名字作出回应。

normal.en: The family runs own, owner, owners and co-ownership.
normal.cn: 同族词包括拥有、所有者、各位所有者与共有。

normal.en: Law separates the right from the holding, which is why possession alone is not ownership.
normal.cn: 法律把权利与占有分开，所以单有占有并不构成所有权。

normal.en: A company can be owned as surely as a field, so the word measures shares as well as soil.
normal.cn: 公司可以像田地一样被拥有，因此这个词既衡量股份，也衡量土地。

normal.en: Modern managers ask staff to take ownership of a problem, which keeps only the sense of treating it as one's own.
normal.cn: 现代管理者要求员工对问题「负起责任」，这里只保留了「把它当作自己的事」这一层。

abstract.en: Picture a brass plate on a door with a name cut into it, and a key hanging from the same hook.
abstract.cn: 想象门上钉着一块刻了名字的铜牌，同一只钩子上挂着钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a register whose page is rewritten, and the right to the house moving with the ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一本登记簿的页面被改写，房屋的权利随墨迹一起转移。

abstract.en: Picture a worker who writes his own name on a task that no one assigned to him.
abstract.cn: 想象一名工人把名字写在一件没有人指派给他的任务上。

examples.en: Ownership of the building was split between two families.
examples.cn: 这栋楼的所有权由两户人家分有。

examples.en: The report recommends wider home ownership among younger households.
examples.cn: 报告建议让更多年轻家庭拥有自有住房。

examples.en: She took ownership of the delay and explained what went wrong.
examples.cn: 她承担了延误的责任，并解释了出错之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧呢事普」——「欧」听成「我」，「呢」听成「的」：写着我的名字的那件东西，就是所有权。

root: 古英语 agan「拥有、占有」+ 古英语 -scipe「形状、状态」→ ownership。两部分均属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；该动词的日耳曼语祖形与更深的印欧语词根都属重构形式，无直接文献实证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a name on a door. The legal right to dispose comes first, then the plain fact of holding, then belonging as a relation; from there the word measures shares, divides public from private regimes, lends itself to personal responsibility, extends to works of the mind, and remembers an older layered tenure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从门上刻着的名字开始。先是对物处置的法律权利，其次是持有的事实，再其次是归属这一关系；由此这个词衡量股份、区分公有与私有、借给个人责任感、延伸到心智作品，并记得一种较早的分层保有权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name on a plate beside a key, marking who may dispose of what is behind the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙旁铜牌上的名字，标明谁有权处置门后之物。

branches.en: RIGHT AND HOLDING: the legal power to dispose, and the bare fact of having something in hand.
branches.cn: 权利与持有：处置的法律权力，以及手中确实有某物的事实。

branches.en: BELONGING: the relation that ties a thing to a name, including the older layered tenure of land.
branches.cn: 归属：把物与名字系在一起的关系，包括较早的分层土地保有权。

branches.en: SHARES: ownership measured in stock, and the position of a firm's proprietor.
branches.cn: 股份：以股票衡量的所有权，以及企业业主的地位。

branches.en: REGIMES: the political division between public and private holding.
branches.cn: 制度：公有与私有之间的政治分野。

branches.en: RESPONSIBILITY AND AUTHORSHIP: treating a task as one's own, and attributing a work to its maker.
branches.cn: 责任与作者身份：把任务当作自己的事，以及把作品归到创作者名下。

intro.en: This family is entirely Germanic: a verb for having plus a native suffix for a condition, with compounds built by adding person and place words.
intro.cn: 这个家族完全是日耳曼语的：一个表示「拥有」的动词，加上一个本族语的表状态后缀，再由表示人与处所的词构成复合形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this family. Latin-based near synonyms such as possession and proprietorship come from different roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个家族没有拉丁语来源。由拉丁语派生的近义词如「占有」与「所有权」出自不同的词根。

items.meaning: the condition of holding something as one's own
items.meaningCN: 把某物作为自己之物持有的状态
items.example: Ownership passed to the buyer on signature.
items.exampleCN: 签署之时所有权转移给买方。

items.example: They own the land beside the river.
The owners met to divide the rent.
items.exampleCN: 各位业主开会分配租金。

items.meaning: a holder of title shared with another
items.example: Each co-owner may use the whole garden.
items.exampleCN: 每位共有人都可以使用整个花园。

items.meaning: title shared by more than one person
items.exampleCN: 共有要求就修缮达成一致。

items.example: The landowner leased the field for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 地主把这块田租了十年。

items.meaning: a person who owns the house he lives in
items.example: Homeowners pay a local property tax.
items.exampleCN: 房主需缴纳地方房产税。

共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）

拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）
